You are given a Quadratic Shortest Path Problem (QSPP).

Problem description:
- The input specifies a directed graph.
- A source node and a target node are given.
- You must choose exactly one directed path from the source node to the target node.

Graph structure:
- The graph is defined by a list of directed edges.
- Each edge record includes (edge_start_node, edge_end_node, edge_id).
- IMPORTANT: edge_id is an EDGE identifier used ONLY for costs. It is NOT a node ID.

Costs:
- Each edge_id has a base (linear) cost.
- Quadratic costs are defined for all ordered pairs (i, j) of edge IDs, including diagonal terms (i == j).
- If both edges i and j are selected in the path, then quadratic_costs[i][j] contributes to the objective.

Objective:
- Minimize: total_cost = (sum of linear costs of selected edges)
            + (sum of quadratic_costs[i][j] over all ordered pairs (i, j) of selected edges).

Input format:
{{INSTANCE_INPUT}}

Return your decision using exactly the following JSON format (no extra keys, no explanations):
```json
{
  "solution": []
}
```
The list `solution` must be a valid directed path expressed as a sequence of **node identifiers only**.
Each entry in the list must be a node ID from the input graph.
The first node must be the given source node, and the last node must be the given target node.
**Do NOT include edge_id (or any edge identifiers) in the solution.**
**Do not include explanations or any extra keys.**

The idea is to pick the one route that ends up with the least total friction by summing all individual frictions and any extra pairwise hits. contexts.text: [BASELINE] Canonical task wording.

As the courier dispatcher, pick a single directed route from the pickup location to the delivery location that follows the available directed streets and keeps the sum of segment charges and any extra fees for using particular pairs of segments as small as possible, noting that each segment also carries an extra fee that applies when it is included.

As a park ranger planning a trek, choose a single directed trail from the trailhead to the overlook that follows the marked directional tracks and minimizes the total of baseline effort per trail segment plus additional penalties for certain pairs of segments that interact, with each segment also having its own use surcharge.

As a network engineer, select a single directed path through the router topology from source node to destination node that follows the directed links and minimizes total latency and extra interference costs incurred by specific pairs of links, while accounting for a per-link usage penalty.

As a factory floor manager, choose a single directed sequence of conveyor segments from the loading station to the packing station that respects the directed flow of the conveyors and minimizes combined energy and setup costs including extra charges when particular segment pairs are both used, and include each segment's usage surcharge.

As a water system planner, pick a single directed channel route from the reservoir inlet to the treatment outfall that follows the directed canal segments and minimizes total pumping and erosion control expenses including additional costs for certain adjacent segment combinations, and include the extra fee tied to each channel segment when it is used.

As a transit planner, determine a single directed path for a bus from the depot to the terminal that follows allowed directed roads and minimizes the sum of fuel and tolls plus any extra costs that arise when specific pairs of road segments are both included, with each road segment also carrying a use-specific charge.

As an electrical designer, pick a single directed wiring route for a signal from the input pad to the output pad that follows the directed circuit routing rules and minimizes overall resistance and crosstalk costs including pairwise coupling penalties, and include the component leakage penalty associated with each used segment.

As a warehouse operator, select a single directed aisle path for a robot from the pick zone to the drop zone that follows the directed aisle flows and minimizes total traversal time and congestion penalties for particular aisle combinations, while also accounting for a fixed time cost for using each aisle segment.

As a shipping coordinator, choose a single directed sea corridor route from the origin port to the destination port that follows the allowed directional lanes and minimizes the total freight charges plus extra handling fees that apply when certain corridor pairs are both used, with each corridor segment also incurring a usage fee.

As an event organizer, plan a single directed path through the exhibit halls from the main entrance to the keynote stage that follows the directed visitor flow and minimizes total walking burden and extra delay penalties for visiting certain paired corridors, and account for a per-corridor obstacle cost when a corridor is included.

As a build engineer, choose a single directed chain of build steps from the source module to the final artifact that follows dependency directions and minimizes total compile time including extra cache miss penalties for particular pairs of steps, and include the per-step overhead that applies when that step is executed.

As an emergency planner, designate a single directed evacuation path from the assembly area to the safe zone that follows the directed exit corridors and minimizes total exposure and bottleneck penalties including additional costs activated when certain corridor pairs are both used, and include any hazard surcharge attached to each corridor used.

As a marketing coordinator, select a single directed sequence of distribution channels from content origin to audience endpoint that follows the directional flow of channels and minimizes total spending including overlap penalties for certain channel pairs, while also considering the activation fee associated with each channel used.

As a drone operator, choose a single directed air corridor path from launch site to landing pad that follows permitted directional corridors and minimizes battery consumption and interference penalties arising from particular corridor pairs, and include the per-corridor wind penalty when that corridor is flown.

As a teacher planning a lesson run, pick a single directed progression of topics from the introductory node to the summary node that follows the allowed prerequisite directions and minimizes total preparation and redundancy costs including extra friction when certain topic pairs are both covered, with each topic also carrying its own preparation overhead.

As a pipeline operator, select a single directed flow path for the product from the intake valve to the delivery manifold that follows the directed pipeline segments and minimizes operational and compression costs including coupling penalties for certain pairs of segments, and include the per-segment maintenance cost that applies when a segment is used.

As an installer, map a single directed cable route from the panel to the outlet that follows the allowed directed conduits and minimizes combined material and signal loss costs including extra interference when certain conduit pairs are both used, while accounting for a connector cost tied to each conduit segment used.

As a tourist, plan a single directed walking itinerary from the city gate to the central plaza that follows the directed pedestrian lanes and minimizes total fatigue and crowding penalties including extra discomfort when certain street pairs are both walked, and include the steepness penalty that applies to each block when it is included.

As a quality inspector, choose a single directed inspection route through the production line from the start station to the final station that follows the directed flow of stations and minimizes total inspection time and transition penalties for certain station pairs, while accounting for the setup time attached to each inspected station.

As an academic adviser, design a single directed course sequence from the introductory seminar to the capstone that follows prerequisite directions and minimizes the total workload and friction costs including extra difficulty when certain course pairs are both taken, and include the administrative fee associated with each course when it is chosen.

As a daily commuter, pick a single directed route from your home to your office following the available one directional streets so that the sum of each street's personal toll and any extra charges that arise when certain streets are used together is as small as possible.

Ask the delivery driver to select a single directed route from the warehouse to the customer that follows the allowed one directional lanes, minimizing the total of per segment fuel cost plus any additional penalties that occur when particular segments are traversed together.

Instruct the network administrator to choose a single directed packet route from the ingress node to the egress node along permissible directed links, minimizing total link transmission cost together with any interaction penalties associated with using certain ordered link pairs.

Tell the commuter cyclist to choose a single directed bike route from the park to the plaza along permitted directional bike lanes that minimizes the total of each lane's expected delay and any additional costs when specific lane sequences occur.

Ask the ferry operator to follow a single directed waterway route from the harbor entrance to the pier using allowed directional channels, aiming to minimize total base passage fees plus any interaction surcharges for particular ordered channel combinations.

Direct the maintenance crew to select a single directed access route from the gate to the machinery room along authorized directed service corridors, minimizing the sum of corridor access cost and any extra charges that happen when specific corridor pairs are both used.

Tell the commuter to pick a single directed subway route from the entry concourse to the destination platform along directed track segments, minimizing total station and segment fees together with any additional penalty that occurs when certain segments are included in the trip.

Ask the plumber to choose a single directed routing of flow from the inlet to the outlet along one directional pipe connections that minimizes the total of individual pipe handling costs and any interaction losses that result from using particular pipe pairs.

Request that the event planner select a single directed guest flow from the lobby to the banquet hall following the venue's directed passageways, minimizing the overall inconvenience cost per passage plus any extra cost from combining specific passages.

Instruct the mail carrier to follow a single directed delivery run from the depot to the mailbox along allowed directional streets, minimizing the total of per street delivery cost and any additional paired penalties when certain streets are traversed together.

Ask the robot operator to program a single directed travel route from the recharge station to the workbench using permitted directed factory lanes, with the objective of minimizing the sum of lane energy use and any interaction penalties for particular ordered lane pairs.

Tell the tourist to select a single directed sightseeing route from the museum entrance to the viewpoint following one directional promenades, minimizing the combined walking effort per promenade and any extra discomfort that arises when specific promenades are taken in combination.

Request that the ambulance driver take a single directed route from the emergency center to the scene along allowed directed streets, minimizing overall travel cost per street plus any additional delay penalties caused by using particular street sequences.

Tell the festival coordinator to plan a single directed supply path from the service gate to the staging area along designated directed thoroughfares, minimizing the total base transport cost per thoroughfare and any extra penalties for specific thoroughfare combinations.

As a web designer, specify a single directed navigation path from the landing page to the checkout page along available link directions, recognizing that each page transition has its own friction cost and some pairs of transitions produce extra combined conversion loss when both are taken, and pick the navigation path that minimizes total friction including those pairwise terms.

As a production planner, route a single directed sequence of machines that a product will visit from initial station to final assembly along permitted flow directions, where each machine hop has an operating cost and certain pairs of hops create extra combined setup cost when both occur, and select the sequence that minimizes the aggregated operating and interaction costs.

As an airline planner, select a single directed series of controlled air corridors from the departure fix to the arrival fix that comply with assigned routing directions, with each corridor leg imposing its own fuel penalty and certain leg pairs generating additional combined penalties when both are flown, and choose the plan that minimizes total fuel and interaction penalties.

As a shopper, choose a single directed course from the store entrance to the checkout following aisle direction signs, with each aisle segment contributing its own walking or time cost and some pairs of segments adding extra combined inconvenience when both are included, and pick the course that minimizes the total inconvenience including those pairwise terms.

As a mailroom operator, send a package along a single directed conveyor path from intake to sorting chute using only allowed belt directions, where each belt segment has an operating cost and certain segment pairs impose extra combined wear when both are used, and route the package to minimize the sum of segment costs and pairwise interactions.

As a security supervisor, assign a single directed patrol route from the guard room to the checkpoint that follows authorized corridor directions, remembering that each corridor adds its own patrol cost and some corridor pairs create extra combined overhead when both are included, and select the route that minimizes total patrol cost including those interactions.

As a data engineer, design a single directed processing pipeline from raw input to final output across available service links, with each link contributing its own computational cost and some pairs of links producing additional combined overhead when both are used, and choose the pipeline path that minimizes the total of individual and interaction costs.

As a hiker planning from the trailhead to the summit, pick a single trail that respects the signposted downhill or uphill directions and minimizes the total of each trail segment’s usual effort plus any extra difficulties that appear when particular segment combinations are taken together.

As a factory robot operator, plan a single motion path from the charging dock to the assembly zone along conveyor directions, choosing the path that yields the lowest total of individual segment operating costs plus pair interaction penalties that occur only if those two segments are used together.

As a traveler booking connecting flights, pick a single sequence of flights from the origin airport to the arrival airport that follows available flight directions, aiming to minimize the sum of each flight’s base cost and the extra fees or delays that occur only when certain flight pairs are chosen together.

As a campus messenger, select a single directed walkway route from the administration building to the research block following posted pedestrian directions, minimizing the combined base effort of each walkway plus extra interaction penalties that occur only when certain walkway pairs are both on the path.

As a tourist planning a walking tour from the square to the viewpoint, pick a single directional path that follows permitted pedestrian flows, choosing the route that minimizes the total of per‑segment fatigue costs and additional pairwise discomforts that only arise when particular segments are used together.

As a film crew coordinator moving gear from the storage room to the set, select a single directed corridor route that follows building traffic rules, minimizing the sum of handling cost for each corridor and any extra interaction costs that are incurred only when certain corridor pairs are both used.

As an operator of a liquid transfer system, pick a single directed pipeline route from the source tank to the destination tank following valve orientations, minimizing the sum of base transfer cost for each segment plus any additional interaction costs that occur only when particular segment pairs are both included.

As a gardener routing irrigation from the main supply to a flower bed, select a single directed hose and valve path that follows allowed flow directions, with the goal of minimizing the sum of per‑section maintenance cost and additional interaction costs that are incurred only when particular section pairs are used together.

Pick a single directed inspection path through the water system from the entry valve to the exit gate, traveling only along permitted flow directions and minimizing the aggregate cost which sums per‑segment inspection time and extra penalties when certain pairs of segments are both inspected, with each segment also imposing its own penalty.

Plan a single directed route for a photographer from the parking area to the lookout that follows permitted path directions and minimizes total tiredness and transit cost by summing per‑path segment effort plus pairwise penalties for segments that interact when both are taken, and include every segment’s individual interaction cost.

Decide on a single directed corridor path for a student moving from the dorm to the lecture hall that follows allowed hallway directions and minimizes overall travel burden by adding each corridor segment base cost and extra interaction costs that arise when particular corridor pairs are both used, with every corridor carrying its own contribution.

Pick a single directed scaffold route for a crew from ground level to the roof that follows permitted assembly directions and minimizes total labor and safety cost where each scaffold segment has a base cost and some ordered pairs of segments create added combined risk when both are installed, including a per‑segment risk cost.

Choose a single directed fiber route from the distribution cabinet to the building that follows permitted conduit directions and minimizes total routing cost by summing each conduit segment base fee and extra interaction fees when particular pairs of segments are both selected, with each segment also incurring its own fee.

Select a single directed sequence of manufacturing stages from raw material intake to finished product that follows allowed process directions and minimizes total production cost by summing baseline cost of each stage and additional interaction costs for stage pairs that are both used, with each stage also contributing its own interaction cost.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.description: Total number of nodes in the directed graph.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.description: Total number of directed edges in the graph.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.description: List of valid node identifiers. The solution path must be an ordered list of node IDs chosen from this list.

global_fields.name: source_node
global_fields.description: Source node ID. The solution path must start at this node.

global_fields.name: target_node
global_fields.description: Target node ID. The solution path must end at this node.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_start_node
edge_item_fields.description: Start (tail) node ID of this directed edge.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_end_node
edge_item_fields.description: End (head) node ID of this directed edge.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_id
edge_item_fields.description: Unique identifier of this directed edge. This ID is used to reference linear costs and quadratic interaction costs.

linear_item_fields.name: edge_id
linear_item_fields.description: Edge identifier. Must match an edge_id listed in the edges section.

linear_item_fields.name: linear_cost
linear_item_fields.description: Base cost incurred if and only if this edge is used in the chosen path.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_i_id
quadratic_item_fields.description: Identifier of the first edge in a quadratic interaction term.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_j_id
quadratic_item_fields.description: Identifier of the second edge in a quadratic interaction term.

quadratic_item_fields.name: quadratic_cost
quadratic_item_fields.description: Additional cost incurred if both edges are used in the path (diagonal terms represent self-interaction).

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of intersections in the city map; used to understand the size of the navigation problem (informational only).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of one-way street segments available on the map; equals the number of directed edges in the graph.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: List of intersection identifiers (place names). The chosen route must be an ordered list of these intersection IDs, starting at the pickup and ending at the delivery.

global_fields.name: source_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the pickup intersection where the route must start.

global_fields.name: target_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the delivery intersection where the route must end.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_start_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The intersection ID where this directed street segment begins (tail of the directed edge). Consecutive intersections in the final route must match these starts and ends.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_end_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The intersection ID where this directed street segment ends (head of the directed edge). This together with segment_start_intersection defines a legal one-way move.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_id
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for this directed street segment. This ID is used only to reference costs (linear and quadratic) and must never appear in the final route output (the output must list intersections only).

linear_item_fields.name: edge_id
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the street segment (must match a segment_id from the edges list); used to link the base charge below to the corresponding segment.

linear_item_fields.name: linear_cost
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: The normal charge (base cost) incurred if this street segment is included in the chosen route. This cost applies once when the segment is used.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_i_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the first street segment in a pairwise combination fee term; matches a segment_id from the edges list.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_j_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the second street segment in a pairwise combination fee term; matches a segment_id from the edges list.

quadratic_item_fields.name: quadratic_cost
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Additional fee incurred if and only if both referenced segments are used on the same route. Diagonal terms (where segment_i_id == segment_j_id) represent an extra per-segment fee that applies when that segment is included; off-diagonal terms are directional combo fees that apply when both segments appear (both directions between a pair, if present, get added separately).

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct places on the park map (e.g., junctions, viewpoints, trailhead, overlook). This is the count of location identifiers the path may use.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of one-way trail segments (directed paths) connecting the locations on the map. Each segment is a possible step along a route from the trailhead to the overlook.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: List of valid location identifiers (place names or IDs). The chosen route must be an ordered list of these locations starting at the trailhead and ending at the overlook.

global_fields.name: source_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the starting location for the trek (the trailhead). The first entry in the output path must match this location.

global_fields.name: target_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the destination location (the overlook). The final entry in the output path must match this location.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_start_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The starting location ID for this directed trail segment (where the segment departs). Consecutive locations in the output path must follow these directed starts and ends.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_end_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The ending location ID for this directed trail segment (where the segment arrives). This, together with the start, defines a legal one-way step on the map.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_id
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for this specific directed trail segment. This ID is used only to reference that segment's base effort and interaction penalties in the cost data (the segment ID itself must not appear in the final location-only path output).

linear_item_fields.name: edge_id
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the trail segment to which the following baseline effort applies. Must match a segment_id from the trail segments list.

linear_item_fields.name: linear_cost
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Baseline effort (or surcharge) for taking this single trail segment. This cost is incurred if and only if the segment is included anywhere in the chosen route.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_i_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the first trail segment in an ordered interaction pair. Ordered pairs are used because the penalty can depend on which segment is considered first.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_j_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the second trail segment in an ordered interaction pair. If both this segment and segment_i are used in the chosen route, this ordered-pair term contributes its penalty.

quadratic_item_fields.name: quadratic_cost
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Extra penalty incurred when both corresponding segments are used in the route. Terms are specified for all ordered pairs (i,j); when i == j this represents an additional per-segment surcharge applied if that segment is used. For two distinct segments the total pairwise penalty is determined by the relevant ordered terms (orientation matters).

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of router nodes in the directed topology. Use this to validate that the provided router list contains the expected count.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of directed links (ordered connections) between routers. This is the count of available directed edges in the network.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: List of valid router identifiers in the topology. The chosen path must be an ordered sequence of these router IDs, starting at the source and ending at the target.

global_fields.name: source_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the starting router for the route. The path must begin at this router.

global_fields.name: target_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the destination router for the route. The path must terminate at this router.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_start_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Tail router of a directed link: the router where this directed connection originates. Consecutive nodes in the output path must match link endpoints.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_end_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Head router of a directed link: the router where this directed connection terminates. This defines a valid hop from link_from_router to link_to_router.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_id
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for this directed link. This ID is used internally to reference the link's base latency and any pairwise interference costs; it must not appear in the solution path output.

linear_item_fields.name: edge_id
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the directed link corresponding to the following per-link latency value. Must match a link_id listed in the edges section.

linear_item_fields.name: linear_cost
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Base latency penalty incurred when this specific directed link is used in the chosen route. This cost is added for each occurrence of the link in the path.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_i_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the first link in a pairwise interference term. If both this link and link_j_id are used in the route, the associated quadratic cost applies.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_j_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the second link in a pairwise interference term. Pair (link_i_id, link_j_id) represents ordered interaction; both directions may be present and are summed if both links are used.

quadratic_item_fields.name: quadratic_cost
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Additional latency or interference hit incurred when both nominated links are used in the selected route. Diagonal entries (where link_i_id equals link_j_id) represent extra per-link interference that applies when that single link is used (in addition to its per_link_latency).

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct locations on the factory floor map (including loading and packing); each location is a node that conveyors connect.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of directed conveyor segments available (each segment is a directed edge you may choose to traverse).

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: List of all valid location identifiers on the factory map. The chosen route must be an ordered sequence of these location IDs.

global_fields.name: source_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the loading station location where the route must start.

global_fields.name: target_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the packing station location where the route must end.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_start_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Location ID at the tail (start) of this directed conveyor segment — where that conveyor segment originates.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_end_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Location ID at the head (end) of this directed conveyor segment — where that conveyor segment delivers to.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_id
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for this conveyor segment (used to reference its base cost and any pairwise surcharges). Note: this ID identifies the segment, not a location.

linear_item_fields.name: edge_id
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the conveyor segment this linear cost applies to; must match a segment_id from the segments list.

linear_item_fields.name: linear_cost
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Base cost charged when this conveyor segment is used on the chosen route (covers energy and one-off usage surcharge for that segment).

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_i_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the first conveyor segment in a pairwise interaction term (ordered pair).

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_j_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the second conveyor segment in a pairwise interaction term (ordered pair).

quadratic_item_fields.name: quadratic_cost
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Additional cost incurred if both referenced conveyor segments are used on the route. Diagonal terms (same segment listed twice) are a surcharge applied when that single segment is used; off-diagonal terms are ordered and both directions may contribute if both corresponding segments appear.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of distinct junctions/locations on the canal map (including source and target). Used to understand the size of the network of canal junctions.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total count of directed canal segments (edges) on the map. Each segment is a possible directed channel piece that can be selected as part of a route.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Ordered list of all valid junction identifiers on the canal map. Any route must be an ordered sequence of these node IDs starting and ending at the specified terminals.

global_fields.name: source_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the reservoir inlet junction where the route must start. The first node in the chosen path must equal this value.

global_fields.name: target_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the treatment outfall junction where the route must end. The last node in the chosen path must equal this value.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_start_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Tail junction ID of this directed canal segment (where the segment begins). Consecutive nodes in the output path must correspond to such start→end pairs.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_end_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Head junction ID of this directed canal segment (where the segment ends). Together with the start node this defines the allowed directed movement along the canal.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_id
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for this canal segment. This ID is used to match the segment to its per-use surcharge and to any pairwise extra fees; it identifies an EDGE, not a node.

linear_item_fields.name: edge_id
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the canal segment to which the following linear charge applies. Must correspond to a segment_id listed in the edges section.

linear_item_fields.name: linear_cost
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Base pumping/erosion plus per-segment surcharge incurred if and only if this canal segment is included in the chosen route.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_i_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the first canal segment in a pairwise interaction term. Used with second_segment_id to look up any extra fee that applies when both segments are used (order matters).

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_j_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the second canal segment in a pairwise interaction term. Together with first_segment_id defines an ordered pair whose joint use triggers the listed extra fee.

quadratic_item_fields.name: quadratic_cost
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Additional cost charged when both referenced segments are included in the same selected route. Diagonal entries (same segment for both IDs) represent an extra per-segment fee applied when that segment is used; off-diagonal entries are ordered pair fees (first→second).

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total count of distinct map locations (intersections, stops, or nodes) on the city map. Used to validate the size of the nodes list and to confirm how many locations exist for routing the bus.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of directed road segments (one-way road pieces) available on the map. Each corresponds to a possible single-step movement the bus can take.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: An ordered list of valid location identifiers (intersection or stop IDs) on the map. The planned route must be a sequence of these location IDs starting at the depot and ending at the terminal.

global_fields.name: source_node
global_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the depot location where the bus trip must start. The first node in the output path must match this ID.

global_fields.name: target_node
global_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the terminal location where the bus trip must end. The final node in the output path must match this ID.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_start_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The location ID where this directed road segment begins (the tail of the directed edge). Consecutive nodes in the chosen path must match these start/end relationships.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_end_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The location ID where this directed road segment ends (the head of the directed edge). This plus the start location defines the allowed one-way connection the bus can take.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_id
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The unique identifier assigned to this directed road segment. This ID is used only to reference that segment's base charge and its interaction costs with other segments (it must not appear in the final output path).

linear_item_fields.name: edge_id
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the road segment to which the base per-use charge applies. This must match a road_segment_id declared in the edges list.

linear_item_fields.name: linear_cost
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: The direct monetary cost (fuel, tolls, per-segment use fees) incurred if and only if the corresponding road segment is included in the chosen route.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_i_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the first road segment in a two-segment interaction term. Quadratic entries reference ordered pairs of segments and are applied when both segments appear on the route.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_j_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the second road segment in a two-segment interaction term. For an ordered pair (i,j) the listed interaction cost applies when both segment i and segment j are used.

quadratic_item_fields.name: quadratic_cost
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: The additional cost charged when both referenced road segments are used on the same route. Diagonal entries (same segment for i and j) represent per-segment extra charges that apply whenever that segment is used.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of physical locations (routing vertices) in the circuit layout; the path must be an ordered sequence of these locations.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of directed wiring segments (directed edges) available in the layout that connect locations.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: List of valid location identifiers (node IDs) in the routing grid. The solution path must be a sequence drawn from these location IDs.

global_fields.name: source_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the starting location for the signal (the input pad). The first node in the returned path must equal this ID.

global_fields.name: target_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the destination location for the signal (the output pad). The last node in the returned path must equal this ID.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_start_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Start (tail) location ID of a directed wiring segment: the location the segment departs from. Consecutive nodes in the path must follow such directed segments.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_end_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: End (head) location ID of a directed wiring segment: the location the segment arrives at. Consecutive nodes in the path must follow such directed segments.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_id
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for a directed wiring segment. This ID links the segment to its leakage/resistance (linear) cost and any pairwise coupling (quadratic) penalties; it identifies segments (not nodes) and must not appear in the output path.

linear_item_fields.name: edge_id
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the wiring segment to which the linear cost applies; must match a segment_id defined among the edges.

linear_item_fields.name: linear_cost
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Base penalty (e.g., leakage or resistance) incurred if and only if the associated wiring segment is included in the chosen route.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_i_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the first wiring segment in a pairwise coupling term. Used together with segment_j_id to reference a coupling penalty that applies if both segments are used.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_j_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the second wiring segment in a pairwise coupling term. Coupling penalties are defined for ordered pairs (i,j); for two distinct segments the total interaction is the sum of the two ordered terms.

quadratic_item_fields.name: quadratic_cost
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Additional penalty (crosstalk/coupling or self-interaction) incurred when both referenced segments are used in the route. Diagonal terms (i == j) represent a self-interaction component associated with that segment.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct warehouse locations (nodes) in the directed aisle network. Used to understand the size of the map of locations the robot may pass through.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of directed aisle segments (edges) in the warehouse layout. Each represents a one-way aisle segment the robot can traverse.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Ordered list of valid location identifiers in the warehouse (e.g., intersections, pick area, drop area). The solution path must be an ordered sequence of these location IDs.

global_fields.name: source_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the starting location where the robot begins (the pick area). The returned path must start at this location.

global_fields.name: target_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the destination location where the robot must end (the drop area). The returned path must end at this location.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_start_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The tail location ID of a directed aisle segment: the location where that aisle segment begins (robot departs this node when taking the segment).

edge_item_fields.name: edge_end_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The head location ID of a directed aisle segment: the location where that aisle segment ends (robot arrives at this node when taking the segment).

edge_item_fields.name: edge_id
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for this directed aisle segment. This ID links the segment to its fixed traversal time and any congestion interaction penalties. (Note: these IDs identify aisle segments, not locations, and must not appear in the final path output.)

linear_item_fields.name: edge_id
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the aisle segment to which the fixed traversal time applies. Must match an aisle_segment_id defined in the edges list.

linear_item_fields.name: linear_cost
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Fixed time cost to traverse the specified aisle segment. This time is incurred if and only if the robot uses that segment on its chosen route.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_i_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the first aisle segment in a pairwise congestion interaction term. Used with aisle_j_id to look up an additional penalty that applies when both segments appear on the chosen route.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_j_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the second aisle segment in a pairwise congestion interaction term. Together with aisle_i_id, defines an ordered pair whose joint use adds the listed congestion penalty to the route time.

quadratic_item_fields.name: quadratic_cost
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Extra time penalty incurred if both referenced aisle segments are used on the same route. Diagonal entries (where aisle_i_id == aisle_j_id) represent an additional per-segment penalty that applies when that single segment is included; off-diagonal ordered pairs add extra congestion time only when both segments appear on the chosen path.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total count of distinct ports (graph nodes) in the sea-lane network. The solution path must select node IDs from this set of ports.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of directed sea corridor segments (edges) connecting ports. Each segment is a one-way lane between two ports.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: List of valid port identifiers in the shipping network. The output path must be an ordered list of these port IDs from origin to destination.

global_fields.name: source_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the origin port where the chosen shipping route must start.

global_fields.name: target_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the destination port where the chosen shipping route must end.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_start_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Start (tail) port ID of a directed corridor segment. This is the port you depart from when using this lane.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_end_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: End (head) port ID of a directed corridor segment. This is the port you arrive at when using this lane.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_id
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for this corridor segment (edge). This ID links the segment to its base tariff and to any pairwise handling fees; note that corridor IDs identify segments and must not appear in the final node-only path output.

linear_item_fields.name: edge_id
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the corridor segment for which a base usage tariff is given. Must match a corridor_id from the edges list.

linear_item_fields.name: linear_cost
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Base freight charge (tariff) incurred if and only if the corresponding corridor segment is used on the chosen route.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_i_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the first corridor segment involved in a pairwise handling-fee term. This references a corridor_id from the edges list.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_j_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the second corridor segment involved in a pairwise handling-fee term. This references a corridor_id from the edges list.

quadratic_item_fields.name: quadratic_cost
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Additional handling fee incurred when both specified corridor segments are used on the same route. Diagonal entries (same corridor_i_id and corridor_j_id) represent an extra fixed charge applied when that single segment is used; for two distinct segments the ordered pair value contributes when both segments appear (the model sums ordered terms as specified).

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct exhibit locations (nodes) in the directed map: includes the lobby, intermediate halls/rooms, and the keynote stage. A valid route is an ordered list of these location IDs.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of directed corridors (one-way hallways) in the map. Each corridor is a directed connection between two locations and is referenced by a unique corridor identifier in the cost data.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The list of all valid location identifiers (room/hall names). The route you output must be an ordered list of IDs chosen from this list, starting at the entrance and ending at the keynote stage.

global_fields.name: source_node
global_fields.scenario_description: The location ID of the main entrance (lobby). The chosen path must begin at this location.

global_fields.name: target_node
global_fields.scenario_description: The location ID of the keynote stage. The chosen path must end at this location.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_start_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The start location ID (tail) of this directed corridor — where a visitor enters this hallway. Consecutive corridor_from/corridor_to pairs must chain to form a valid directed path.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_end_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The end location ID (head) of this directed corridor — where a visitor exits this hallway.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_id
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The unique identifier for this corridor (edge). This ID is used only in the cost tables (linear and quadratic) to index corridor-specific walking and interaction costs. Corridor IDs identify corridors for cost computation and must not appear in the final output path (which must list only location IDs).

linear_item_fields.name: edge_id
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: The corridor identifier that this base walking cost applies to. Must match a corridor_id from the edges list.

linear_item_fields.name: linear_cost
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: The base walking burden (distance/time/effort) incurred if and only if this corridor is included in the chosen route. This cost is added once per corridor used on the path.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_i_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the first corridor in a pairwise interaction term. Quadratic interaction costs are indexed by ordered corridor pairs to model extra delays when certain corridors are both used.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_j_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the second corridor in a pairwise interaction term. Using both corridor_i_id and corridor_j_id in the route triggers an additional cost described by the quadratic_cost entry (ordered interactions are allowed).

quadratic_item_fields.name: quadratic_cost
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: The extra delay/penalty incurred if both specified corridors are included in the chosen path. For diagonal entries where corridor_i_id == corridor_j_id this represents a per-corridor obstacle cost that is incurred when that corridor is used. For distinct corridors i and j, the full extra penalty when both are used equals pair_delay_cost for (i,j) plus the pair_delay_cost for (j,i) (ordered contributions).

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of modules (graph nodes) in the build dependency graph. This tells you how many module locations exist in the directed dependency network you may traverse from the root module to the final artifact.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of directed dependency edges in the graph (each edge represents a possible build step that advances from one module to another).

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: List of module identifiers (node IDs). The solution path must be an ordered sequence of these module IDs beginning at the source module and ending at the final artifact, and each adjacent pair must follow a directed dependency edge.

global_fields.name: source_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the root module (source). The chosen build chain must start at this module.

global_fields.name: target_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the final artifact module (target). The chosen build chain must end at this module.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_start_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Module ID where this directed dependency (build step) starts — the prerequisite module that must be built before moving to the next module along this edge.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_end_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Module ID where this directed dependency (build step) ends — the module produced or reached after performing this build step.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_id
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for this directed build step (the edge). This ID ties the edge to its compile time and any pairwise cache-miss penalties. Note: this ID labels edges only and must not appear in the final output path (which uses module IDs only).

linear_item_fields.name: edge_id
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Reference to the build_step_id for which the linear cost applies. Use this to match a specific directed build step to its base compile time and per-step overhead.

linear_item_fields.name: linear_cost
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Base compile time (including the per-step overhead) incurred if and only if the referenced build step is executed as part of the chosen chain. This is added once per included edge.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_i_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the first build step in a pairwise interaction. This links to a build_step_id and, together with step_j_id, indicates a cache-miss penalty that applies when both steps appear in the chosen chain.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_j_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the second build step in a pairwise interaction. The ordered pair (step_i_id, step_j_id) may incur a penalty that depends on both steps and their order in the chain.

quadratic_item_fields.name: quadratic_cost
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Additional compile-time penalty incurred if both referenced build steps are present in the selected chain. For diagonal entries (step_i_id == step_j_id) this represents an extra self-overhead when that step runs; for distinct ordered pairs the penalty may be asymmetric and both directions contribute separately when both edges are used.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct rooms or locations in the building map. The solver should understand this as the count of nodes in the directed corridor network connecting the assembly area to the safe zone.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of one-way exit corridors in the building. Each corridor is a directed edge connecting two rooms and has its own hazard surcharge and interactions with other corridors.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: List of valid room identifiers (node IDs). Any proposed evacuation route must be an ordered sequence drawn from this list, starting at the assembly area and ending at the safe zone.

global_fields.name: source_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the assembly area room where evacuees start. The chosen directed path must begin at this room.

global_fields.name: target_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the safe zone room where evacuees finish. The chosen directed path must end at this room.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_start_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The start (tail) room ID of a directed corridor. This indicates the room you leave when you traverse this corridor in the path.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_end_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The end (head) room ID of a directed corridor. This indicates the room you enter when you traverse this corridor in the path.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_id
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for the corridor (directed edge). This ID is used to reference the corridor's hazard surcharge and any pairwise penalties, but corridor IDs must not appear in the final node-only path output.

linear_item_fields.name: edge_id
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Reference to a corridor identifier (must match a corridor_id defined in the corridor list). Used to link the following hazard surcharge to the correct corridor.

linear_item_fields.name: linear_cost
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Base exposure cost (hazard surcharge) incurred if and only if the referenced corridor is used on the chosen evacuation path. This is a per-corridor additive cost.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_i_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the first corridor in a quadratic interaction term. This refers to a specific directed corridor whose joint usage with corridor_j_ref may trigger an extra penalty.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_j_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the second corridor in a quadratic interaction term. For ordered pairs, the extra penalty may depend on which corridor comes before the other; both ordered terms combine for distinct corridors.

quadratic_item_fields.name: quadratic_cost
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Additional penalty incurred when both referenced corridors are present on the chosen route. Diagonal terms (where corridor_i_ref equals corridor_j_ref) represent an extra surcharge applied if that single corridor is used; for two distinct corridors both ordered terms apply (i,j and j,i) if both appear on the path.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct locations/stages in the distribution map (e.g., servers, platforms, channels). Each location is a node that can appear in the chosen one-way chain from content origin to audience endpoint.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of directed channel hops (one-way connections) available between locations. Each hop represents a possible single-step transition in a distribution chain.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: List of all valid location identifiers (node IDs). The final solution must be an ordered sequence of these locations starting at the content origin and ending at the audience endpoint.

global_fields.name: source_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the starting location where the content originates. The chosen distribution chain must start at this node.

global_fields.name: target_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the final target location representing the audience endpoint. The chosen distribution chain must end at this node.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_start_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The tail (start) location ID for this directed channel hop — where this one-way transition begins in the distribution flow.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_end_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The head (end) location ID for this directed channel hop — where this one-way transition delivers the content.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_id
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for this directed channel hop. This ID is used to reference the hop's activation fee and any overlap penalties with other hops (do not output these IDs in the final path).

linear_item_fields.name: edge_id
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Channel hop identifier that must match a channel_hop_id listed in the edges section; used to tie the activation fee to a specific hop.

linear_item_fields.name: linear_cost
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Base activation fee charged if and only if the corresponding channel hop is used in the selected chain. Sum these fees for every hop in the chosen route.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_i_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the first channel hop in an overlap penalty term. When this hop and a second hop are both used, this term may contribute an additional asymmetric overlap cost.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_j_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the second channel hop in an overlap penalty term. The pair (channel_i_id, channel_j_id) denotes an ordered interaction whose cost applies if both hops appear in the chosen chain.

quadratic_item_fields.name: quadratic_cost
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Additional cost incurred when both channel_i_id and channel_j_id are included in the selected chain. These penalties are ordered/asymmetric: if two distinct hops i and j are used, add overlap_penalty(i,j) and overlap_penalty(j,i). Diagonal terms (i == j) represent any extra per-hop surcharge or self-interaction that applies when that single hop is used.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct locations (waypoints, junctions, or named positions) in the directed air-corridor network. Used to understand the size of the airway graph.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of directed air corridors (one-way corridors) available in the network. Each corridor corresponds to a directed edge with its own penalties.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Ordered list of valid location identifiers (node IDs). The chosen drone route must be an ordered sequence drawn from these location IDs, starting at the launch site and ending at the landing pad.

global_fields.name: source_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the launch location (source node). The output path must begin at this named location.

global_fields.name: target_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the landing pad (target node). The output path must end at this named location.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_start_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Start location (tail) of this directed air corridor: the node ID where this one-way corridor departs.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_end_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: End location (head) of this directed air corridor: the node ID where this one-way corridor arrives.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_id
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for this specific directed corridor. This ID links the corridor to its linear and quadratic penalty values. Note: corridor_id identifies a corridor (edge) and must not appear in the final node-only path output.

linear_item_fields.name: edge_id
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the corridor to which the linear (per-corridor) battery/wind penalty applies. Must match a corridor_id defined in the edges list.

linear_item_fields.name: linear_cost
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Base penalty (battery and wind cost) incurred if and only if the corresponding corridor is flown on the chosen route. This value is added once per used corridor.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_i_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the first corridor in an ordered interaction pair. This references a corridor_id for which an interaction penalty may apply when flown together with corridor_j_id.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_j_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the second corridor in an ordered interaction pair. If both corridor_i_id and corridor_j_id are used on the route, the listed interaction penalty applies (ordering may matter).

quadratic_item_fields.name: quadratic_cost
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Additional penalty incurred if both referenced corridors are used on the selected path. Diagonal terms (same corridor for i and j) represent an extra built-in penalty for using that single corridor.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of topics in the lesson map. Each topic is a node; this count tells how many distinct topic nodes exist.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of allowed directed transitions between topics. Each transition represents a valid prerequisite-followup step you can take in the lesson sequence.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for all topics. The chosen lesson sequence must be an ordered list of these topic IDs from the intro to the wrap-up.

global_fields.name: source_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the introductory topic where the lesson run must start.

global_fields.name: target_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the summary/wrap-up topic where the lesson run must end.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_start_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The topic you must have just covered before taking this transition — the tail of the directed transition (the prior topic in sequence).

edge_item_fields.name: edge_end_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The topic you move to when you take this directed transition — the head of the transition (the next topic in sequence).

edge_item_fields.name: edge_id
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for this directed transition (edge). Use this ID to reference the transition when assigning prep costs and interaction (redundancy/friction) costs.

linear_item_fields.name: edge_id
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the transition whose base preparation overhead is given. Matches one of the transition_id values from the transitions list.

linear_item_fields.name: linear_cost
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Base preparation time or effort incurred if and only if this transition is used in the lesson sequence. This models the individual prep burden associated with taking the transition (covering the next topic in that context).

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_i_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the first transition in an interaction term. When both this transition and the second transition are used in the chosen lesson sequence, the listed quadratic cost applies (ordered pair may matter).

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_j_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the second transition in an interaction term. Paired with the first transition to describe extra redundancy, overlap, or awkwardness that arises if both transitions (and thus the topics they involve) are included in the same lesson run.

quadratic_item_fields.name: quadratic_cost
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Additional prep time or friction incurred if both referenced transitions are present in the final lesson sequence. Diagonal terms (same transition for i and j) represent any extra fixed overhead associated with including that single transition.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of physical locations (junctions, valves, manifolds) in the pipeline network. These are the node IDs that may appear in the chosen route from the intake valve to the delivery manifold.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of directed pipeline segments (individual pipe pieces or connections) in the network. Each segment is a directed edge that can be used in a route.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: List of all valid location identifiers in the pipeline (e.g., intake, intermediate junctions, delivery). The solution path must be an ordered list of these location IDs starting at the intake valve and ending at the delivery manifold.

global_fields.name: source_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the intake valve location where the batch originates. The selected path must start at this location.

global_fields.name: target_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the delivery manifold location where the batch must end. The selected path must terminate at this location.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_start_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Start (tail) location identifier for this directed pipeline segment. Indicates where this pipe piece begins in the flow direction.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_end_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: End (head) location identifier for this directed pipeline segment. Indicates where this pipe piece delivers flow in the flow direction.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_id
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for this directed pipeline segment. This ID is used to reference the segment's linear and quadratic cost terms in the cost data (note: segment IDs must not appear in the final path output).

linear_item_fields.name: edge_id
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the pipeline segment whose per-use linear fee is given. Must match a segment_id listed in the edge (segments) section.

linear_item_fields.name: linear_cost
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Per-segment cost incurred if this pipeline segment is included in the chosen route. This represents the segment's base operational/compression cost combined with the per-segment maintenance surcharge that applies when the segment is used.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_i_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the first pipeline segment in an ordered coupling term. Used together with segment_j_id to identify a pair whose joint use can create an extra coupling penalty.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_j_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the second pipeline segment in an ordered coupling term. Paired with segment_i_id; ordering matters because coupling charges can be direction-dependent.

quadratic_item_fields.name: quadratic_cost
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Additional cost incurred if both referenced segments are used in the same route. For ordered distinct segments, if both are used the total added penalty includes the coupling_cost for (i,j) plus the coupling_cost for (j,i). For diagonal terms (i == j), this represents an extra self-interaction charge applied when that single segment is used.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct physical locations in the conduit network (including the panel and the outlet). This counts nodes in the directed conduit graph and helps verify the set of location IDs.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of directed conduit segments available to route the cable. Each segment is a directed edge in the graph and corresponds to one physical conduit piece or run.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Ordered list of valid location identifiers (node IDs) in the building's conduit network. The chosen route must be an ordered sequence of these location IDs starting at the panel and ending at the outlet.

global_fields.name: source_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the panel location (the route must start at this node). This is the origin node in the directed conduit graph.

global_fields.name: target_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the outlet location (the route must end at this node). This is the destination node in the directed conduit graph.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_start_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The tail (start) location ID of a directed conduit segment: where that conduit segment begins (from which you travel along this directed piece).

edge_item_fields.name: edge_end_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The head (end) location ID of a directed conduit segment: where that conduit segment leads (the next location reached when using this directed piece).

edge_item_fields.name: edge_id
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for this directed conduit segment. This ID is used to reference the segment's base connector/material fee and any interaction penalties with other segments. (Note: segment IDs identify conduit pieces, not locations, and must not appear in the final node-only route output.)

linear_item_fields.name: edge_id
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the conduit segment whose base cost is given. Must match a conduit_segment_id declared in the conduit segments list.

linear_item_fields.name: linear_cost
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Base cost for using this conduit segment (material + connector cost). This cost is incurred if and only if the segment is included in the chosen route.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_i_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the first conduit segment in an ordered interaction term. Used together with second_conduit_segment_id to describe an interference or extra-loss cost that applies when both segments are used in the route.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_j_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the second conduit segment in an ordered interaction term. Interaction costs are directional, so the ordered pair (first, second) can represent a different contribution than (second, first).

quadratic_item_fields.name: quadratic_cost
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Additional cost incurred when both referenced conduit segments are used in the same route. For diagonal terms where the two identifiers are the same, this represents an extra per-segment penalty beyond the base cost (e.g., extra handling or signal loss tied to that segment). For distinct segments, this models ordered interference or coupling; the full extra cost from using both segments is the sum of the two ordered contributions.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total count of distinct map locations (intersections, landmarks, or corners) in the pedestrian network; used to understand the size of the map for the stroll from the city gate to the central plaza.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total count of directed pedestrian blocks (one-way street segments) in the map; each block is a possible step along a walking route.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Ordered list of valid location identifiers (node IDs) on the map. The chosen walking itinerary must be a sequence of these locations, starting at the city gate and ending at the central plaza.

global_fields.name: source_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the starting location for the walk — the city gate. The output path must begin at this location.

global_fields.name: target_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the destination for the walk — the central plaza. The output path must end at this location.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_start_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The location identifier where this directed block (street segment) begins (the tail of the block). Consecutive blocks in the itinerary must connect end-to-start by these location IDs.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_end_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The location identifier where this directed block (street segment) ends (the head of the block). This defines the allowed one-way movement along that block.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_id
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for this specific directed block. This identifier links the block to its base tiredness (steepness) penalty and to any pairwise extra discomfort when combined with other blocks.

linear_item_fields.name: edge_id
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of a specific block (must match a block_identifier listed under edges). This links the block to its base fatigue and steepness penalty.

linear_item_fields.name: linear_cost
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Base fatigue (and any per-block steepness penalty) incurred when this block is included in the chosen route. This cost is counted once for each block used.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_i_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the first block in a pairwise awkwardness term. If both this block and the second block are used on the route, the specified extra discomfort applies.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_j_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the second block in a pairwise awkwardness term. Used together with the first_block_identifier to define extra discomfort when both blocks appear on the same itinerary.

quadratic_item_fields.name: quadratic_cost
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Additional discomfort penalty incurred if both referenced blocks are included in the chosen path. Diagonal terms (both identifiers equal) represent an extra self-penalty applied when that single block is used.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of stations in the production-line map. The inspector must choose a path that visits a sequence of these stations from the start to the final station.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of directed transitions (allowed conveyor/inspection moves) between stations. Each transition is a directed link the inspector can follow.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: List of valid station identifiers (nodes). The inspection route must be an ordered list of these station IDs that form a valid directed path.

global_fields.name: source_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the starting station where the inspection route must begin.

global_fields.name: target_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the final station where the inspection route must end.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_start_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Start (tail) station ID for this directed transition — the station the inspector departs from when taking this move.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_end_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: End (head) station ID for this directed transition — the station the inspector arrives at when taking this move.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_id
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for this directed transition. This ID is used to link the transition to its base time and any pairwise penalties; it identifies a transition (edge), not a station.

linear_item_fields.name: edge_id
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the directed transition (must match a transition_id from the transitions list) for which the base time is given.

linear_item_fields.name: linear_cost
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Base time incurred if the inspector uses this transition. This represents the travel time along the link plus the setup time associated with inspecting the station reached by that transition (i.e., the per-transition base inspection/travel time).

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_i_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the first transition in an ordered pair. Used to specify an ordered pairwise slowdown that applies when both transitions are used on the chosen route.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_j_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the second transition in an ordered pair. Together with transition_i_id this defines an ordered interaction (order may matter) that adds extra time if both transitions appear on the route.

quadratic_item_fields.name: quadratic_cost
