quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Additional time penalty incurred if both specified transitions are used on the inspection route. For ordered pairs (i,j) this penalty applies when transition i and transition j are both in the path (diagonal terms i==j represent an extra per-transition setup or self-interaction cost applied when that transition is used).

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct courses (nodes) available in the prerequisite graph. Use this to understand the size of the curriculum from which the single course sequence must be drawn.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of directed prerequisite links in the graph. Each link corresponds to a specific enrollment step (an edge) that represents taking a course that advances you from one course to the next.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The list of valid course identifiers (node IDs). The final output path must be an ordered list of these course IDs starting at the intro seminar and ending at the capstone, and every consecutive pair must match a directed prerequisite link.

global_fields.name: source_node
global_fields.scenario_description: The course ID for the introductory seminar where the sequence must start. The output path's first node must equal this ID.

global_fields.name: target_node
global_fields.scenario_description: The course ID for the capstone where the sequence must end. The output path's last node must equal this ID.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_start_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The course ID at the tail of this directed prerequisite link — the prerequisite course you must have taken before taking the successor. This describes the 'from' node of the enrollment step.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_end_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The course ID at the head of this directed prerequisite link — the course you enroll in after satisfying the prerequisite. This describes the 'to' node of the enrollment step.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_id
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for this specific prerequisite link (edge). In this scenario the identifier denotes the particular course-taking step associated with that directed link. NOTE: this ID refers to an edge (a course-taking action), not a course node, and edge identifiers must not appear in the final node-only path output.

linear_item_fields.name: edge_id
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: The unique identifier of the prerequisite link (edge) to which the linear cost applies. This matches a prereq_link_id declared in the edges list and denotes the specific course-taking step whose base workload and administrative fee are being charged if that step is included in the chosen sequence.

linear_item_fields.name: linear_cost
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: The base cost incurred when that particular prerequisite link (i.e., taking that course at that step) is included in the chosen path. Interpreted as the normal workload for the course plus the administrative fee for enrolling in it. This cost is counted once for each edge used in the path.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_i_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the first prerequisite link in an ordered pair for a pairwise friction term. This refers to the specific course-taking step i whose interaction with step j may impose extra difficulty when both are taken.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_j_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the second prerequisite link in an ordered pair for a pairwise friction term. This refers to the specific course-taking step j whose interaction with step i may impose extra difficulty when both are taken.

quadratic_item_fields.name: quadratic_cost
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: The additional cost incurred if both referenced prerequisite links (course-taking steps) are included in the chosen path. Diagonal terms (where edge_i_id == edge_j_id) represent any extra burden a single course imposes on itself beyond its base workload (for example, a course that is unusually time-consuming by itself). Off-diagonal terms represent extra friction or difficulty that arises only when both courses are taken (note: ordered pairs may be asymmetric, so taking A then B can differ from taking B then A). For two distinct edges i and j the total pairwise contribution is the sum of the (i,j) and (j,i) entries when both edges are used.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of intersections (distinct locations) in the one-way street map between home and office. Use this to understand the map size.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of directed streets (one-way roads) on the map. Each represents a possible street segment you may take.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: List of intersection identifiers. The chosen route must be an ordered list drawn from these intersection IDs, starting at home and ending at the office.

global_fields.name: source_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of your home intersection. The returned path must start at this intersection.

global_fields.name: target_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of your office intersection. The returned path must end at this intersection.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_start_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Start intersection (tail) of this directed one-way street — where you enter this street segment.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_end_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: End intersection (head) of this directed one-way street — where this street segment leads.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_id
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for this specific one-way street segment used to reference its base toll and any interaction fees. (This ID identifies a street, not an intersection, and must not appear in the final node-only route output.)

linear_item_fields.name: edge_id
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Reference to the street identifier whose base toll is being specified. Must match a street_id listed in the edges section.

linear_item_fields.name: linear_cost
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Base monetary cost (toll) charged if and only if the corresponding street is included in the chosen route.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_i_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the first street in an interaction rule. Used together with street_j_ref to look up any extra fee triggered when both streets are used on the same route.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_j_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the second street in an interaction rule. Interaction fees are defined for ordered pairs (street_i_ref, street_j_ref), including when both identifiers are the same.

quadratic_item_fields.name: quadratic_cost
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Additional fee incurred when both referenced streets are included on the chosen route. For diagonal entries (same street_i_ref and street_j_ref) this is an extra self-charge for using that street; for distinct streets the ordered pair fee contributes and ordered pairs combine (both directions may apply as described in the scenario).

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of intersections (nodes) on the street map. Used to understand the size of the delivery network.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of directed road segments (one-way lanes) available between intersections in the map.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The list of valid intersection identifiers. The driver’s chosen route must be an ordered sequence of these intersection IDs.

global_fields.name: source_node
global_fields.scenario_description: The intersection ID where the delivery starts (the warehouse). The route must begin at this intersection.

global_fields.name: target_node
global_fields.scenario_description: The intersection ID of the delivery destination (the customer). The route must end at this intersection.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_start_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The intersection ID at the tail of a directed road segment — the intersection you depart from when taking this one-way segment.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_end_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The intersection ID at the head of a directed road segment — the intersection you arrive at when taking this one-way segment.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_id
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for this directed road segment (used to reference costs). Note: segment IDs identify segments only and must not appear in the final intersection-only route output.

linear_item_fields.name: edge_id
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the road segment to which this base fuel cost applies; must match a segment_id from the edges list.

linear_item_fields.name: linear_cost
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Base fuel/operating cost incurred if the driver uses this road segment as part of the chosen route (applies only when the segment is included).

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_i_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the first road segment in a pairwise penalty term. When both this segment and the segment_j_id segment are used, an extra penalty may apply.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_j_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the second road segment in a pairwise penalty term. Paired with segment_i_id to define a conditional additional cost if both segments are traversed.

quadratic_item_fields.name: quadratic_cost
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Additional penalty charged if and only if both referenced segments are used in the route. Diagonal terms (where segment_i_id == segment_j_id) represent an extra single-segment penalty for taking that specific segment; ordered pairs are allowed so using two segments can incur both directions' penalties.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of network locations (graph nodes) available for routing. All node IDs in the 'nodes' list come from this set; the chosen path must use IDs drawn from these locations.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of directed physical links (edges) in the network. This counts one-way transmission links; each link has a unique link identifier used elsewhere to refer to its costs.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The list of valid location identifiers (node IDs) in the network. The output path must be an ordered sequence of IDs from this list, starting at the ingress and ending at the egress.

global_fields.name: source_node
global_fields.scenario_description: The starting location (entry point) for the packet route. The first node in the reported path must equal this ingress node.

global_fields.name: target_node
global_fields.scenario_description: The destination location (exit point) for the packet route. The last node in the reported path must equal this egress node.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_start_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The tail (start) location ID of a directed network link. This must match one of the location_ids and denotes where that one-way link departs.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_end_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The head (end) location ID of a directed network link. This must match one of the location_ids and denotes where that one-way link arrives.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_id
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The unique identifier for this directed link (edge). This identifier is used in the cost tables to refer to the link’s base cost and its ordered interaction costs with other links. NOTE: link identifiers reference edges only and must never appear in the final path output (the output must list node IDs only).

linear_item_fields.name: edge_id
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: The unique link identifier that this base (linear) cost applies to. Must match a link_identifier defined in the edge list.

linear_item_fields.name: linear_cost
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: The base transmission charge incurred if and only if the corresponding directed link is included in the chosen route.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_i_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: The first link’s identifier in an ordered pair. Used together with ordered_link_j_id to look up an ordered interaction penalty that applies when both links are used on the same route.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_j_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: The second link’s identifier in an ordered pair. The pair (ordered_link_i_id, ordered_link_j_id) denotes an ordered interaction: the penalty applies if both links appear on the chosen path (order matters).

quadratic_item_fields.name: quadratic_cost
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: The additional penalty charged when both links in the ordered pair are used on the chosen path. Diagonal terms (where ordered_link_i_id == ordered_link_j_id) represent extra cost incurred simply for including that single link.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct places (intersections, landmarks, or decision points) on the bike-map; used to know how many place names exist to form routes from the park to the plaza.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of directed bike lanes (one-way segments) on the map; each represents a possible directed step a cyclist can take between places.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The list of valid place identifiers (names) on the map. Any route you output must be an ordered sequence drawn from this list, starting at the park and ending at the plaza.

global_fields.name: source_node
global_fields.scenario_description: The place identifier corresponding to the route start (the park). The solution path must begin at this place.

global_fields.name: target_node
global_fields.scenario_description: The place identifier corresponding to the route end (the plaza). The solution path must finish at this place.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_start_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The place (tail) where this directed bike lane begins — the origin intersection or landmark for that one-way lane.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_end_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The place (head) where this directed bike lane ends — the destination intersection or landmark for that one-way lane.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_id
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The unique identifier (code) for this specific directed bike lane. This code refers to a lane (edge) and is used to look up its base delay and interactions; lane codes must not appear in the final route output, which should list only place names.

linear_item_fields.name: edge_id
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: The lane code identifying which one-way lane the base (linear) expected delay applies to; must match a lane_code from the edges list.

linear_item_fields.name: linear_cost
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: The base expected delay (in the same units throughout) incurred if the cyclist uses this lane on the chosen route. Add these for every lane included in the path.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_i_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: The lane code for the first lane in a pairwise interaction term. If both this lane and the paired lane are used on the route, the specified extra delay applies (diagonal means the lane's self-interaction).

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_j_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: The lane code for the second lane in a pairwise interaction term. When both this lane and lane_i are included in the route, this interaction contributes additional delay.

quadratic_item_fields.name: quadratic_cost
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: The extra delay incurred when both lanes identified by lane_i_code and lane_j_code are used in the chosen route. Diagonal entries (same lane for i and j) represent an extra cost that applies simply by including that lane.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct harbor locations (nodes) in the navigation map — includes the harbor entrance, intermediate waypoints/channels endpoints, and the pier. Used to understand the size of the map.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of directed one-way water channels (edges) available for routing the ferry. Each channel is a permissible directed passage between two harbor locations.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: List of all valid location identifiers in the harbor (e.g., entrance, buoys, docks, pier). The chosen route must be an ordered sequence of these location IDs, starting at the harbor entrance and ending at the pier.

global_fields.name: source_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the harbor entrance location where the ferry trip must start. The first node in the output path must match this ID.

global_fields.name: target_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the pier location where the ferry trip must end. The last node in the output path must match this ID.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_start_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The start (tail) location ID of this directed water channel — where the ferry enters this channel.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_end_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The end (head) location ID of this directed water channel — where the ferry exits this channel.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_id
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for this directed channel. This ID is used only in the fee and surcharge tables to reference channels; it must not appear in the final location-only route output.

linear_item_fields.name: edge_id
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Reference to the channel identifier (must match a channel_id from the channels list) for which the base passage fee is specified.

linear_item_fields.name: linear_cost
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Base passage fee charged if and only if the ferry uses the referenced channel during its trip. This fee is added once per used channel in the total cost.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_i_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the first channel in an ordered pair used to specify a surcharge term. Matches a channel_id from the channels list.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_j_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the second channel in an ordered pair used to specify a surcharge term. Matches a channel_id from the channels list.

quadratic_item_fields.name: quadratic_cost
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Additional surcharge applied if both channels in the ordered pair (first_channel_id, second_channel_id) end up being used in the chosen trip. Diagonal terms (same channel for both IDs) represent a self-interaction added when that channel is used; for two distinct channels both ordered surcharges (i,j) and (j,i) contribute if both are used.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct locations (rooms, junctions, or points) in the plant layout. Used to understand the size of the map the maintenance crew can traverse.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of one-way service corridors (directed corridors) connecting locations. Each corridor is a selectable segment of the crew's route.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The list of valid location identifiers (node IDs) in the facility. The chosen route must be an ordered list of these location IDs, starting at the gate and ending at the machinery room.

global_fields.name: source_node
global_fields.scenario_description: The location ID corresponding to the guarded gate where the maintenance crew starts. The first node in the output path must equal this ID.

global_fields.name: target_node
global_fields.scenario_description: The location ID corresponding to the machinery room where the crew must finish. The final node in the output path must equal this ID.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_start_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The location ID at the tail (start) of this one-way service corridor — where the crew enters this corridor segment.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_end_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The location ID at the head (end) of this one-way service corridor — where the crew exits this corridor segment.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_id
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The unique internal identifier for this corridor segment, used to reference its access charge and any pairwise surcharge. (This ID refers to the corridor itself and must not appear in the final node-only route output.)

linear_item_fields.name: edge_id
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: The corridor identifier that this base access charge applies to. Must match a corridor_id listed in the corridors (edges) section.

linear_item_fields.name: linear_cost
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: The base charge (including any per-corridor surcharge) incurred if the maintenance crew uses this corridor in their chosen route. Added once for each used corridor.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_i_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the first corridor in an ordered pair whose joint use may trigger an extra fee. Order matters: this is the 'first' corridor in the ordered interaction.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_j_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the second corridor in an ordered pair whose joint use may trigger an extra fee. Together with corridor_i_id, it defines an ordered interaction whose cost applies only if both corridors are used.

quadratic_item_fields.name: quadratic_cost
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: The additional fee charged if both corridors corridor_i_id and corridor_j_id appear in the chosen route. For i == j this is a self-surcharge applied when that single corridor is used; for i != j both ordered terms (i,j) and (j,i) contribute if both corridors are used.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct station locations and intermediate concourse points in the directed subway map; used only to describe the size of the network.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of one-way track segments (directed edges) connecting stations; each corresponds to a single billable segment in the route.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: List of valid station identifiers (including entry concourse and destination platform). The chosen route must be an ordered list of these station IDs, starting at the entry concourse and ending at the destination platform.

global_fields.name: source_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the entry concourse station where the commuter starts. The output path must begin with this station ID.

global_fields.name: target_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the destination platform station where the commuter ends the trip. The output path must end with this station ID.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_start_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Start station ID (tail) for this directed track segment — the station you depart from when taking this one-way segment.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_end_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: End station ID (head) for this directed track segment — the station you arrive at when taking this one-way segment.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_id
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for this track segment used to look up its base fee and any pairwise penalties. This ID identifies a segment for cost calculations but must not appear in the final station-only output.

linear_item_fields.name: edge_id
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Track segment identifier that matches one of the segment_id values above; used to associate the following base charge with that specific segment.

linear_item_fields.name: linear_cost
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Base fee (station/segment charge and any single-segment surcharge) incurred if and only if the corresponding track segment is included on the chosen route.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_i_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the first track segment in a pairwise penalty term; used together with segment_j_id to determine an extra penalty that applies only if both segments are on the chosen route.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_j_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the second track segment in a pairwise penalty term; paired with segment_i_id to define an additional cost incurred only when both segments are used on the route.

quadratic_item_fields.name: quadratic_cost
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Additional penalty amount applied when both specified segments are included in the commuter's route. For diagonal entries where segment_i_id equals segment_j_id, this is an extra cost that applies whenever that single segment is used.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of junctions (locations) in the plumbing network. Use this to understand the size of the maze of pipes; solution path must list node IDs chosen from the junction_ids list.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of directed pipe segments in the network. Each pipe is a one-way connection between two junctions and has its own handling cost and identifier.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: List of valid junction identifiers (node IDs). The route must be an ordered list of these junction IDs beginning at the inlet_junction and ending at the outlet_junction.

global_fields.name: source_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the inlet junction where the plumber must start the flow route. The chosen path must begin at this junction.

global_fields.name: target_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the outlet junction where the plumber must end the flow route. The chosen path must terminate at this junction.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_start_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The upstream junction ID (tail) where this directed pipe segment begins. Consecutive nodes in the solution must follow these directed connections.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_end_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The downstream junction ID (head) where this directed pipe segment ends. This defines the allowed direction of travel for that pipe.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_id
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for this directed pipe segment. This ID is used exclusively to reference the pipe's base handling fee and any interaction losses with other pipes (it must NOT appear in the output path).

linear_item_fields.name: edge_id
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the pipe whose base handling fee is given. Must match a pipe_id listed among the pipes; if the route uses that pipe, its base fee applies once.

linear_item_fields.name: linear_cost
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Base handling cost (fee) incurred if and only if that pipe is included in the chosen route. Add this once per used pipe.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_i_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the first pipe in an interaction term. Quadratic terms describe extra losses that occur when specific pipes are used together (ordered interactions are possible).

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_j_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the second pipe in an interaction term. When both pipe_i_id and pipe_j_id appear on the selected route, this term contributes an extra loss.

quadratic_item_fields.name: quadratic_cost
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Additional loss (penalty) incurred if both referenced pipes are used on the chosen route. Diagonal terms (where pipe_i_id equals pipe_j_id) represent a self-interaction loss for using that single pipe; off-diagonal ordered pairs both contribute when the two pipes are present.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct locations/points in the venue map (rooms, intersections, or corridor endpoints). This tells how many node identifiers exist for planning the single route from the lobby to the banquet hall.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of one-way corridors (directed passageways) in the venue. Each corridor is a possible segment of the guest flow and has its own costs.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: List of valid location identifiers (node IDs) in the venue. The chosen route must be an ordered sequence of these location IDs starting at the lobby and ending at the banquet hall.

global_fields.name: source_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the lobby location where all guests start. The first element of the output path must equal this node ID.

global_fields.name: target_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the banquet hall location where all guests must arrive. The last element of the output path must equal this node ID.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_start_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The starting location ID (tail) of this directed corridor — where guests enter this corridor segment.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_end_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The ending location ID (head) of this directed corridor — where guests exit this corridor segment.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_id
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for this specific corridor (directed edge). This ID is used to reference its base inconvenience and interactions with other corridors in the cost data.

linear_item_fields.name: edge_id
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Reference to the corridor identifier whose base inconvenience is described on this line. Must match a corridor_id defined in the corridors list.

linear_item_fields.name: linear_cost
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: The basic inconvenience cost of using this corridor (e.g., narrowness, length, awkwardness). This cost is incurred if and only if the corridor is included in the chosen route.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_i_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the first corridor in an interaction pair. When both this corridor and the corridor_j_id are used on the chosen route, an additional interaction cost (possibly directional) may apply.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_j_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the second corridor in an interaction pair. The interaction cost entry applies if both corridor_i_id and this corridor_j_id appear on the final route.

quadratic_item_fields.name: quadratic_cost
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Additional inconvenience incurred when both referenced corridors are used on the route. Diagonal terms (same corridor for i and j) represent extra friction from using that single corridor; off-diagonal ordered pairs represent extra friction that arises when that ordered pair of corridors appears together (the total pair contribution to the overall objective is the sum of both ordered entries when two distinct corridors are used).

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct locations on the town map (intersections, addresses, or landmarks). The route must reference only these locations.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of directed one-way streets available for the delivery run. Each street is a directed connection between two locations.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: List of valid location identifiers (names or IDs for intersections/places). The delivered path must be an ordered sequence drawn from these identifiers.

global_fields.name: source_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the depot where the mail carrier starts. The first location in the returned path must match this depot.

global_fields.name: target_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the mailbox (delivery endpoint). The last location in the returned path must match this mailbox.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_start_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Start location (tail) of this directed street: the location you depart from when you traverse this one-way street.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_end_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: End location (head) of this directed street: the location you arrive at when you traverse this one-way street.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_id
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for this directed street. This ID is used only to reference costs (linear and quadratic) and must never appear in the final path output (the output lists locations only).

linear_item_fields.name: edge_id
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the street whose base delivery cost is given. Must match a street_id from the streets list.

linear_item_fields.name: linear_cost
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Base cost to serve/traverse this street, incurred if and only if the mail carrier uses that street on the route.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_i_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the first street in a paired penalty term. Used together with street_j_id to look up the extra cost that applies when both streets appear on the run.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_j_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the second street in a paired penalty term. For two distinct streets, the total pair penalty includes both ordered terms (i,j) and (j,i). When i == j this represents an extra charge that applies if that single street is used.

quadratic_item_fields.name: quadratic_cost
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Additional penalty applied if both referenced streets are included in the chosen route. For diagonal entries (same street), this is an extra per-street charge; for distinct streets, ordered entries combine to form the full interaction penalty.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total count of distinct factory locations (nodes) on the map; includes the recharge station and the workbench and every intermediate location the robot may visit.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of directed factory lanes (directed edges) available for routing the robot from the recharge station to the workbench.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The list of valid location identifiers (node IDs) in the factory. The solution must be an ordered sequence of these location IDs starting at the recharge station and ending at the workbench, with each consecutive pair connected by a permitted directed lane.

global_fields.name: source_node
global_fields.scenario_description: The location identifier for the robot's charger; the route must start at this location.

global_fields.name: target_node
global_fields.scenario_description: The location identifier for the robot's workbench; the route must end at this location.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_start_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The start (tail) location ID of a directed factory lane. Each lane goes from this tail location to its head location in the given direction.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_end_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The end (head) location ID of a directed factory lane. A valid consecutive pair of locations in the answer must match some lane tail->head pair.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_id
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The unique identifier for a specific directed lane. This ID is used to reference that lane's energy cost and any ordered interaction penalties; note that lane IDs identify lanes, not locations, and must not appear in the final location-only route output.

linear_item_fields.name: edge_id
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the directed lane whose base energy consumption is given. If the chosen path uses this lane, its linear (energy) cost applies once.

linear_item_fields.name: linear_cost
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: The base energy cost incurred when the robot uses the corresponding directed lane on its trip from the recharge station to the workbench.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_i_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the first lane in an ordered lane-pair penalty. If both this lane and the second_lane_id are used in the path (in any positions), this term contributes to the total cost according to the defined ordering rules.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_j_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the second lane in an ordered lane-pair penalty. When both this lane and first_lane_id are used in the chosen route, the quadratic_cost (for the ordered pair) is added to the total.

quadratic_item_fields.name: quadratic_cost
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: The extra penalty (positive or zero) applied when both lanes identified by first_lane_id and second_lane_id appear on the chosen route. Diagonal terms (first_lane_id == second_lane_id) represent a self-interaction cost for using that lane.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct locations (nodes) on the promenade map, including the museum entrance and the viewpoint; used to understand the size of the map.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of one-way promenades (directed edges) between locations; tells how many directed walkway segments are available to choose from.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: List of valid location identifiers (node IDs) such as 'entrance', 'square', 'viewpoint'; the chosen solution must be an ordered sequence of these location IDs from source to target following one-way promenades.

global_fields.name: source_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the museum entrance location (the path must start here); this is the start node for the single allowed sightseeing route.

global_fields.name: target_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the viewpoint location (the path must end here); this is the destination node for the single allowed sightseeing route.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_start_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The start location (tail) of a directed promenade: the place you are at before walking this one-way segment.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_end_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The end location (head) of a directed promenade: the place you arrive at after taking this one-way segment.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_id
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for this promenade segment (used internally to reference its linear and quadratic costs). Note: this ID refers to an edge only and must not appear in the final node-only path output.

linear_item_fields.name: edge_id
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Promenade identifier matching an 'edge_id' in the edges list; links the linear walking effort value to a specific one-way promenade.

linear_item_fields.name: linear_cost
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Base walking effort cost incurred if and only if the corresponding promenade is included in the chosen route; this is added once per used promenade.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_i_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the first promenade in an ordered pair for an interaction term; used with promenade_j_id to define extra discomfort when both promenades appear on the route.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_j_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the second promenade in an ordered pair for an interaction term; paired with promenade_i_id to specify directional interaction discomfort added when both segments are used.

quadratic_item_fields.name: quadratic_cost
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Additional discomfort cost incurred if and only if both promenades (promenade_i_id and promenade_j_id) are taken on the same route. Diagonal terms (i == j) represent extra awkwardness associated with taking that promenade at all.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total count of distinct locations (intersections or landmarks) in the map. The ambulance route will choose a sequence of these locations from the emergency center to the incident.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of directed one-way streets available on the map. Each street is a directed connection the ambulance may travel along.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: List of valid location identifiers (nodes). The output path must be an ordered list of these location IDs, starting at the emergency center and ending at the incident scene.

global_fields.name: source_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the starting location where the ambulance is based. The first entry in the returned route must equal this location ID.

global_fields.name: target_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the destination location where the incident is. The final entry in the returned route must equal this location ID.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_start_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Location identifier where this directed street begins (the tail of the directed edge). Consecutive locations in the route must connect via such start→end street definitions.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_end_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Location identifier where this directed street ends (the head of the directed edge). The route may move from the start to this end when selecting that street.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_id
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for this directed street. This ID is used to reference the street's base travel time and any interaction (delay) terms with other streets; note that street IDs themselves must not appear in the final route output.

linear_item_fields.name: edge_id
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the street whose base travel time is being specified. Must match a street_id from the streets list.

linear_item_fields.name: linear_cost
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Basic travel time (minutes or seconds) incurred if the ambulance uses this street in the chosen route. This time is included once per use of the street.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_i_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the first street in a pairwise delay interaction. Used together with street_j_id to specify an added delay incurred if both streets appear on the selected route.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_j_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the second street in a pairwise delay interaction. When both this street and street_i_id are used on the route, the specified interaction delay applies.

quadratic_item_fields.name: quadratic_cost
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Additional delay incurred if both referenced streets are used on the route. For diagonal terms where the two street IDs are the same, this represents an extra penalty associated with using that single street (e.g., known slow segment). For distinct streets, the cost is applied when both appear on the route and both ordered terms (i,j) and (j,i) contribute as defined.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct locations (places, intersections, or sites) in the festival grounds map. This tells the solver how many nodes exist in the directed one‑way thoroughfare network.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of directed one‑way thoroughfares (permitted supply pathways) on the map. Each thoroughfare is a directed link that can be used between two locations.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The list of valid location identifiers (IDs) for all nodes on the map. Any returned route must be an ordered sequence of these location IDs from the service gate to the staging area.

global_fields.name: source_node
global_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the service gate location where the supply route must start. The first entry of the chosen location sequence must equal this ID.

global_fields.name: target_node
global_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the staging area (the stage service point) where the supply route must end. The last entry of the chosen location sequence must equal this ID.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_start_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The location ID at the tail of a directed thoroughfare (the place supplies depart from along this one‑way link). Consecutive locations in the output must match these directed connections.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_end_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The location ID at the head of a directed thoroughfare (the destination of that one‑way link). Each consecutive pair of locations in the route must correspond to an existing thoroughfare from its start to its end.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_id
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The internal unique identifier for this directed thoroughfare used to reference its base transport charge and any interaction penalties. This identifier is for cost data only and must not be printed in the final location sequence output.

linear_item_fields.name: edge_id
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: The internal identifier of the thoroughfare to which the base transport cost applies. This must match a thoroughfare_id declared in the edges list.

linear_item_fields.name: linear_cost
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: The normal (linear) cost charged if that thoroughfare is included anywhere in the chosen supply route. These base charges sum for every thoroughfare used.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_i_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: The internal identifier of the first thoroughfare in an ordered interaction pair. Used together with thoroughfare_j_id to specify an extra penalty applied if both thoroughfares appear on the chosen route.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_j_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: The internal identifier of the second thoroughfare in an ordered interaction pair. The interaction penalty applies when both this thoroughfare and thoroughfare_i_id are included in the final route. Ordered pairs matter; both directions may be present as separate entries.

quadratic_item_fields.name: quadratic_cost
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: The extra penalty charged if both referenced thoroughfares are used in the same supply route. Diagonal entries (where the two thoroughfare IDs are the same) represent an additional self‑interaction charge incurred when that thoroughfare is used.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of web pages in the site map. Use this to understand the size of the navigation graph (includes landing and checkout).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of directed links (clickable transitions) between pages. Each link is a possible single click from one page to another.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: List of page identifiers (page IDs) that can appear in the navigation path. The final solution must be an ordered list drawn from these page IDs.

global_fields.name: source_node
global_fields.scenario_description: The page ID for the landing page where the user starts. The chosen navigation path must begin at this page.

global_fields.name: target_node
global_fields.scenario_description: The page ID for the checkout page where the user must end. The chosen navigation path must terminate at this page.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_start_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The page ID where this directed link (click) starts — the origin page a user is on before clicking this link.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_end_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The page ID where this directed link (click) leads — the destination page the user arrives at after clicking this link.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_id
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique internal identifier for this specific directed link (transition). This identifies the transition for associating its baseline friction and any pairwise interaction costs. Note: link identifiers are for cost bookkeeping only and must NOT appear in the final output path (which should list only page IDs).

linear_item_fields.name: edge_id
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: The same unique link identifier used above to associate a baseline click friction with a particular link/transition.

linear_item_fields.name: linear_cost
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Baseline friction cost (conversion loss) incurred if the user takes this specific link. This cost applies exactly when that link is included in the chosen path.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_i_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the first link in a pairwise interaction. If both this link and the second link are used anywhere on the same chosen path, the listed pairwise cost applies (order can matter).

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_j_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the second link in a pairwise interaction. When both this link and the first link are present in the final path, the pairwise cost contributes to total friction (quadratic interactions are ordered; separate entries may exist for reversed order).

quadratic_item_fields.name: quadratic_cost
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Additional friction (conversion loss) incurred when both links specified by the pair are used in the chosen path. Diagonal entries (where the two identifiers are the same) represent an extra standalone penalty for using that single link.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct stations or machine locations in the production flow network. Used to understand the graph size and validate node identifiers when planning a route from start to finish.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of allowed directed machine-to-machine moves (edges). Each move represents a permitted one-way transfer of the product between two stations.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: List of valid station identifiers (node IDs). The chosen production sequence must be an ordered subset of these IDs, starting at the start station and ending at the final assembly station.

global_fields.name: source_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the initial station where the product begins. The planned path must start at this station.

global_fields.name: target_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the final assembly station where the product must end. The planned path must terminate at this station.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_start_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The tail station ID for this directed move: the machine/station the product departs from when performing this move.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_end_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The head station ID for this directed move: the machine/station the product arrives at when performing this move.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_id
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for this specific directed machine-to-machine move. This ID is used to reference the move's operating cost and any pairwise setup interactions; it should not appear in the final node-only route output.

linear_item_fields.name: edge_id
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the move (must match a move_id listed in the moves/edges section). Refers to the single-move operating cost below.

linear_item_fields.name: linear_cost
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Base operating cost incurred if and only if the corresponding move is used in the chosen production route. Sum these for every move included in the path.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_i_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the first move in a pairwise setup interaction. Used together with move_j_id to determine additional setup cost if both moves occur on the selected route.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_j_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the second move in a pairwise setup interaction. The extra setup cost applies when both move_i_id and move_j_id are used in the final path.

quadratic_item_fields.name: quadratic_cost
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Additional setup cost incurred when both referenced moves are included in the chosen route. Diagonal terms (move_i_id == move_j_id) represent an extra standalone setup cost that applies if that single move is used.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of navigation fixes (waypoints) in the routing network. This counts all distinct fixes that can appear in a valid corridor routing from departure to arrival.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of directed controlled corridor legs available between fixes. Each corridor is a one-way leg that can be flown if its direction matches the routing.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: List of all valid fix identifiers (departure/arrival/waypoints). The chosen routing must be an ordered subsequence of these fixes, starting at the departure_fix and ending at the arrival_fix.

global_fields.name: source_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the departure fix where the routing must start. The first node in the output path must match this fix.

global_fields.name: target_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the arrival fix where the routing must end. The last node in the output path must match this fix.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_start_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Start (tail) fix of a directed corridor leg. In a valid routing, flying this corridor means the path includes this fix immediately before the corridor's end fix.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_end_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: End (head) fix of a directed corridor leg. A corridor from corridor_from_fix to corridor_to_fix is flown if the path contains these two fixes consecutively in that order.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_id
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for this directed corridor leg. This ID links the corridor to its fuel penalty and any pairwise interaction penalties; note that corridor_leg_id identifies a corridor leg (edge) and must never be printed in the final fix-only routing output.

linear_item_fields.name: edge_id
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the corridor leg whose base fuel penalty is specified. Must match a corridor_leg_id defined in the edge list.

linear_item_fields.name: linear_cost
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Base fuel penalty (linear cost) incurred if and only if the corresponding corridor leg is flown as part of the routing.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_i_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the first corridor leg in a pairwise interaction penalty. Used together with corridor_leg_j_id to specify an extra combined penalty when both legs are flown.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_j_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the second corridor leg in a pairwise interaction penalty. The penalty applies only if both corridor_leg_i_id and corridor_leg_j_id are included in the chosen routing.

quadratic_item_fields.name: quadratic_cost
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Additional fuel/penalty amount incurred when both referenced corridor legs are flown. Diagonal terms (same leg for i and j) represent a self-interaction penalty that applies when that single leg is used.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct store locations or junctions in the directed layout (e.g., aisle intersections, end caps). This counts every node in the map including the entrance and the checkout; the solver should expect that the path visits a sequence of these locations.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of directed aisle segments (one-way walking pieces) in the store layout. Each segment is a directed edge you may traverse following aisle direction signs.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: List of valid location identifiers (node IDs) representing points in the store such as ends of aisles or intersections. The solution path must be an ordered list of these location IDs starting at the entrance and ending at checkout.

global_fields.name: source_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the store entrance location where the shopper starts the route. The chosen path must begin at this location.

global_fields.name: target_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the checkout location where the shopper finishes the route. The chosen path must end at this location.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_start_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The start (tail) location ID for this directed aisle segment — where you step onto this segment when following the store arrows.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_end_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The end (head) location ID for this directed aisle segment — where the segment leads to when walked in the allowed direction.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_id
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for this directed aisle segment (edge). This ID is used to reference the segment in the cost tables (linear and quadratic). Note: segment IDs identify edges, not nodes, and must not be included in the final node-only path output.

linear_item_fields.name: edge_id
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the aisle segment to which the base walking/time cost applies. Must match a segment_id listed in the edges section; if the segment is included in the chosen path, this linear cost is added to the total inconvenience.

linear_item_fields.name: linear_cost
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Base inconvenience cost (e.g., walking time, distance, or discomfort) incurred if and only if the corresponding aisle segment is traversed on the chosen route.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_i_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the first aisle segment in a pairwise interaction term. Used together with segment_j_id to look up an extra penalty that applies when both segments appear on the same route.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_j_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the second aisle segment in a pairwise interaction term. For two distinct segments i and j, if both are used the total added quadratic penalty includes the term for (i,j) and the term for (j,i) as listed. Diagonal entries (i == j) represent a self-interaction cost incurred when that single segment is used.

quadratic_item_fields.name: quadratic_cost
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Additional inconvenience cost incurred when both referenced aisle segments are included in the same route. For ordered pair (i,j) this is the cost added when both segment_i_id and segment_j_id are used; the overall pairwise contribution for two distinct segments is the sum of the (i,j) and (j,i) entries.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct facility locations (nodes) in the conveyor layout — every node is a physical place the package can appear at along a continuous belt route.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of directed belt segments (edges) that connect locations in the conveyor system; each segment is a one-way belt the package can travel along.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: List of valid location identifiers in the mailroom (e.g., intake, junctions, sorting chute). The solution path must be an ordered sequence of these locations.

global_fields.name: source_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the intake location where the package enters the conveyor system; the returned path must start at this location.

global_fields.name: target_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the sorting chute location where the package must end up; the returned path must terminate at this location.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_start_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Start (tail) location identifier for this belt segment — the package leaves this location when it traverses this segment.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_end_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: End (head) location identifier for this belt segment — the package arrives at this location after traversing the segment.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_id
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for this specific belt segment. This ID links the segment to its operating cost and to any pairwise wear interactions; note that belt IDs must not appear in the final node-only path output.

linear_item_fields.name: edge_id
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the belt segment whose base operating cost is being specified; must match a belt_segment_id from the edges list.

linear_item_fields.name: linear_cost
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Running cost incurred if this belt segment is used on the chosen route (added once per segment included in the path).

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_i_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the first belt segment in a wear-interaction term; used together with belt_j_id to determine extra combined wear if both segments appear on the route.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_j_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the second belt segment in a wear-interaction term; the interaction is ordered, so belt_i_id followed by belt_j_id can differ from the reverse.

quadratic_item_fields.name: quadratic_cost
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Additional wear cost incurred if both referenced belt segments are used on the same route. Diagonal terms (same belt_i_id and belt_j_id) represent extra self-wear applied when that single segment is used.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of distinct locations (rooms, intersections, or waypoints) in the building map. Use this to understand the size of the corridor network you may traverse.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of directed corridors (one-way hallways or doorways) connecting locations. Each corridor is a possible step along a patrol route.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: List of valid location identifiers (IDs) in the building. A feasible patrol route must be an ordered list of these location IDs starting at the guard room and ending at the checkpoint.

global_fields.name: source_node
global_fields.scenario_description: The location ID of the guard room where the patrol must start. The chosen route must begin at this location.

global_fields.name: target_node
global_fields.scenario_description: The location ID of the checkpoint the patrol must reach. The chosen route must end at this location.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_start_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The starting location ID (tail) of a directed corridor. In a valid route, this location must be immediately before the corridor's end location.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_end_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The ending location ID (head) of a directed corridor. Consecutive locations in the output path must correspond to such corridor start→end pairs.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_id
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for this directed corridor (the corridor object). This ID links the corridor to its base patrol cost and any interaction costs; corridor IDs themselves must not be printed in the final path output.

linear_item_fields.name: edge_id
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Reference to the corridor (must match a corridor_id from the corridors list). This ties a base patrol cost to that specific corridor.

linear_item_fields.name: linear_cost
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: The base cost (effort, time, or resource) incurred if and only if the referenced corridor is included in the chosen patrol route.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_i_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the first corridor in an ordered pair used to specify an interaction overhead. Matches a corridor_id from the corridors list.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_j_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the second corridor in an ordered pair used to specify an interaction overhead. Matches a corridor_id from the corridors list.

quadratic_item_fields.name: quadratic_cost
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Additional overhead incurred if and only if both referenced corridors are used in the patrol. For diagonal entries where corridor_i_id == corridor_j_id, this represents an extra self-overhead for using that single corridor.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of physical or logical locations in the processing map (the number of conveyor stations or service endpoints available).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of directed service links (conveyor belts or processing links) that move the package forward between locations.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: List of all location identifiers (pickup points, intermediate stations, and delivery points). The chosen route must be an ordered sequence drawn from these locations.

global_fields.name: source_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the starting location where the raw input (package) enters the conveyor network. The route must begin here.

global_fields.name: target_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the final destination location where the processed output must arrive. The route must end here.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_start_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The origin location (tail) of a specific directed link / conveyor belt — where an item is placed onto this belt.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_end_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The destination location (head) of that directed link / conveyor belt — where the item exits that belt.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_id
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique code identifying this specific directed link (conveyor/process link). This code is used only to reference that link's individual fee and interactions in the cost tables; it must not appear in the final location-only route.

linear_item_fields.name: edge_id
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: The unique code of the link whose single-link processing fee is being specified. Must match a link_code listed in the edges section.

linear_item_fields.name: linear_cost
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: The base processing/handling fee charged if that specific link (conveyor belt) is used on the chosen route.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_i_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Code of the first link in a pairwise interaction term. When both this link and the second link are used, their combined overhead may apply.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_j_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Code of the second link in a pairwise interaction term. Paired with link_i_code to identify the two links whose joint overhead is defined.

quadratic_item_fields.name: quadratic_cost
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Extra handling/coordination cost incurred when both specified links are used on the same route. Diagonal entries (same link_i_code and link_j_code) represent a small self-surcharge charged if that link is used.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct locations on the mountain map (e.g., trail junctions, trailhead, viewpoints, summit). This tells you how many node identifiers exist in the map of one-way trails.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of directed trail segments (one-way signposted routes) between locations. Each segment is a directed connection a hiker can take following posted uphill/downhill directions.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The list of valid location identifiers (node IDs) on the mountain. The chosen continuous route must be an ordered sequence of these location IDs starting at the trailhead and ending at the summit.

global_fields.name: source_node
global_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the starting location (trailhead). The selected route must begin at this node and follow the directed, signposted segments from here.

global_fields.name: target_node
global_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the destination location (summit). The chosen route must end at this node after following a continuous sequence of one-way trail segments.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_start_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The start (tail) location ID of a directed trail segment — where the hiker steps onto this particular one-way segment. Consecutive segments in the route must match end-to-start accordingly.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_end_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The end (head) location ID of a directed trail segment — where the hiker emerges after traversing this one-way segment. Must match the next segment's start if segments are chained.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_id
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The unique identifier for this directed trail segment used to reference its effort and interactions. Note: this identifies a trail segment for cost accounting and must not appear in the final output path (only location IDs are output).

linear_item_fields.name: edge_id
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Reference to the unique identifier of a trail segment (must match a segment_id from the edges list). This links the usual effort value to that specific one-way segment.

linear_item_fields.name: linear_cost
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: The usual effort (base cost) required to traverse the referenced trail segment — incurred if and only if that segment is included in the chosen route.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_i_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the first trail segment in a pairwise interaction term. Used together with segment_j_id to indicate an extra difficulty that arises when both specific segments are taken on the same route.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_j_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the second trail segment in a pairwise interaction term. The interaction applies only if both this segment and segment_i_id are included on the chosen route (order matters because interactions are defined for ordered pairs).

quadratic_item_fields.name: quadratic_cost
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Additional trouble or extra effort incurred when both referenced segments are used on the same route. Diagonal terms (segment_i_id == segment_j_id) represent self-interaction costs for using that single segment.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total count of distinct locations (nodes) in the conveyor network map the robot may visit when traveling from the charging dock to the assembly zone.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of directed conveyor segments (edges) in the facility; each segment is a possible motion step for the robot.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: List of all valid location identifiers (node IDs) in the factory layout. The chosen route must be an ordered subsequence of these locations, starting at the dock and ending at the assembly area.

global_fields.name: source_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the charging dock location where the robot starts its single continuous trip.

global_fields.name: target_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the assembly zone location where the robot must end its single continuous trip.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_start_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The start location (tail node) of this directed conveyor segment — the node where the robot would be before traversing this segment.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_end_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The end location (head node) of this directed conveyor segment — the node where the robot arrives after traversing this segment.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_id
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for this conveyor segment (edge). This ID is used to reference the segment's operating cost and any pairwise penalties; note that segment IDs themselves must not appear in the final route output (only node IDs).

linear_item_fields.name: edge_id
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the conveyor segment to which the following base operating cost applies. Must match a conveyor_segment_id from the edges list.

linear_item_fields.name: linear_cost
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Base operating cost incurred if and only if the robot uses this conveyor segment in the chosen route (e.g., energy, wear, or time cost for that segment).

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_i_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the first conveyor segment in a pairwise interaction penalty term. When both this segment and segment_j_id are used on the route, the specified penalty applies (as part of an ordered pair).

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_j_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the second conveyor segment in a pairwise interaction penalty term. For distinct segments, penalties are applied for both ordered pairs (i,j) and (j,i) if both segments are used; for i==j this represents a self-penalty for using that single segment.

quadratic_item_fields.name: quadratic_cost
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Additional penalty added to the total route cost if both referenced conveyor segments are used. For ordered pair (i,j) this value is added when both segments appear on the route; when two different segments i and j are both used, both interaction_penalty(i,j) and interaction_penalty(j,i) contribute. Diagonal terms (i==j) represent extra cost incurred solely from using that segment.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of airports (distinct locations) in the flight network — the count of valid airport nodes that can appear on an itinerary.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of directed flights (available legs) in the schedule — the count of distinct one-way flights connecting airports.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: List of airport identifiers (codes) that can appear on an itinerary. The chosen route must be an ordered sequence of these airport codes, starting at the origin and ending at the destination.

global_fields.name: source_node
global_fields.scenario_description: The starting airport code for the itinerary. The output path must begin at this airport.

global_fields.name: target_node
global_fields.scenario_description: The final arrival airport code for the itinerary. The output path must end at this airport.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_start_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The departure airport code for this specific directed flight (the flight's tail). Consecutive airports in the itinerary must match these departures and arrivals for each chosen flight.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_end_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The arrival airport code for this specific directed flight (the flight's head). It defines where that flight lands and which airport can follow next on the itinerary.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_id
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for this flight (this directed edge). This flight_id is used to reference the flight's base fare and any pairwise extra fees with other flights; it identifies the flight itself, not an airport.

linear_item_fields.name: edge_id
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Reference to a flight_id (must match one from the flights list). This links the base fare entry to the specific flight it applies to.

linear_item_fields.name: linear_cost
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: The base ticket cost for this flight. This amount is added to the itinerary total if and only if that flight is included in the chosen route.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_i_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the first flight in a pairwise interaction. Used together with flight_j_id to specify an extra fee or delay that applies if both flights appear on the same itinerary.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_j_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the second flight in a pairwise interaction. When both flight_i_id and flight_j_id are on the chosen route, the listed extra applies.

quadratic_item_fields.name: quadratic_cost
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Additional cost (fee or delay penalty) incurred when both referenced flights are included in the itinerary. Diagonal entries (same flight_i_id and flight_j_id) represent a self-interaction surcharge counted if that single flight is used; for two distinct flights both ordered entries may contribute to the total when both are selected.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct campus locations (nodes) in the directed walkway map. Used to understand the size of the navigation problem from the administration building to the research block.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of directed walkway segments (edges) on the campus map. Each segment follows one-way pedestrian arrows and is a candidate for inclusion in a messenger route.

global_fields.name: nodes
