global_fields.scenario_description: List of valid campus location identifiers (node IDs). The chosen route must be an ordered sequence of these location IDs starting at the administration building and ending at the research block.

global_fields.name: source_node
global_fields.scenario_description: The node ID corresponding to the administration building where the messenger starts. The solution path must begin at this location.

global_fields.name: target_node
global_fields.scenario_description: The node ID corresponding to the research block where the messenger must arrive. The solution path must end at this location.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_start_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The start (tail) location ID of a directed walkway segment — where the messenger steps onto that segment following posted one-way arrows.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_end_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The end (head) location ID of a directed walkway segment — where the messenger arrives after traversing that segment.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_id
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for this specific directed walkway segment. This ID is used to reference the segment's baseline effort and any interaction penalties in the cost data (do not output these IDs in the final path).

linear_item_fields.name: edge_id
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the walkway segment to which the baseline effort applies. Must match a walkway_segment_id from the edges list.

linear_item_fields.name: linear_cost
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: The base effort (linear cost) required to traverse this walkway segment; incurred if and only if the messenger's chosen route includes that segment.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_i_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the first walkway segment in a pairwise interaction term. Used with segment_j_ref to determine an extra penalty if both segments appear on the chosen route.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_j_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the second walkway segment in a pairwise interaction term. Together with segment_i_ref, it identifies a pair whose simultaneous use may add an extra penalty to the route cost.

quadratic_item_fields.name: quadratic_cost
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Additional penalty incurred when both referenced walkway segments are included in the same route. If segment_i_ref equals segment_j_ref, this value is the standalone extra penalty for using that single segment in addition to its baseline effort.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct places (squares, intersections, viewpoints, or other locations) shown on the walking map. This tells you how many node identifiers exist to choose from when listing the route.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of permitted directed walking segments (one‑way legs) between places. Each corresponds to a legal pedestrian move that follows the one‑way signs.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The list of place identifiers (the named locations you can visit). The solution path must be an ordered sequence of these place IDs, starting at the square and ending at the viewpoint.

global_fields.name: source_node
global_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the starting place (the square). The chosen path must begin at this place.

global_fields.name: target_node
global_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the destination place (the viewpoint). The chosen path must end at this place.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_start_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The place identifier where this directed walking leg starts (the tail of the directed edge). Consecutive places in your output must match such starts and ends.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_end_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The place identifier where this directed walking leg ends (the head of the directed edge). This indicates the permitted one‑way direction you may follow on that leg.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_id
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for this directed walking leg (used internally to reference costs). Note: this ID identifies a leg (edge) and must not be printed in the final node sequence output.

linear_item_fields.name: edge_id
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Reference to the unique identifier of a walking leg (must match a leg_identifier from the edges list). This links the base fatigue cost to a particular directed leg.

linear_item_fields.name: linear_cost
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: The base tiredness (linear) cost incurred if and only if that walking leg is used in the chosen route. Sum these for every leg you include in the path.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_i_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the first walking leg in a pairwise discomfort interaction (ordered reference). Used together with second_leg_id_ref to determine extra discomfort when both legs are included in the route.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_j_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the second walking leg in a pairwise discomfort interaction (ordered reference). The pair (first, second) may contribute extra discomfort only if both legs appear in the chosen path.

quadratic_item_fields.name: quadratic_cost
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Additional discomfort cost incurred when both referenced legs are used in the route. Diagonal entries (same leg for both references) represent an extra self‑discomfort that applies if that single leg is used.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct locations (rooms, junctions or places) in the building plan relevant to the move. Used only to describe graph size.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of one-way corridors (directed connections) in the building that the crew can use to move equipment.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: List of valid location identifiers (names or numbers) in the building. The chosen route must be an ordered sequence of these location IDs, starting at the storage area and ending at the shooting area.

global_fields.name: source_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the storage room where the move starts. The first node in the output path must equal this storage location.

global_fields.name: target_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the shooting set where the move ends. The last node in the output path must equal this set location.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_start_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Location identifier where this one-way corridor begins (the corridor's tail). Consecutive nodes in the chosen route must follow such starts and ends.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_end_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Location identifier where this one-way corridor ends (the corridor's head). The route may traverse this corridor only by listing corridor_from then corridor_to consecutively in the path.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_id
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for this corridor used to reference its handling charge and any interaction fees. Note: corridor IDs refer to corridors only and must never appear in the final path output of location IDs.

linear_item_fields.name: edge_id
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the corridor whose base handling charge is specified. This must match a corridor_id from the edges list.

linear_item_fields.name: linear_cost
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Base handling charge incurred if and only if the crew uses that corridor in the chosen route (applies per corridor used).

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_i_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the first corridor in an interaction term. If both this corridor and corridor_j_id are used on the route, the specified interaction_fee applies (order matters when asymmetric).

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_j_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the second corridor in an interaction term. Paired with corridor_i_id to define an extra fee incurred only when both corridors appear on the chosen route.

quadratic_item_fields.name: quadratic_cost
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Additional cost incurred when both corridor_i_id and corridor_j_id are used on the same route. Diagonal terms (same corridor for i and j) represent an extra self-interaction charge incurred when that single corridor is used; off-diagonal terms may differ by order (i then j vs j then i).

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of tanks (nodes) in the one-way pipeline network; the operator’s route will visit a sequence of these tanks from the source to the receiving tank.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of directed pipeline segments (one-way hops through valves) available in the network; each segment connects a pair of tanks in a specific direction.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Ordered list of valid tank identifiers. Any solution must be a sequence of these tank IDs starting at the source_tank and ending at the receiving_tank, with each consecutive pair connected by a directed pipeline segment.

global_fields.name: source_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the starting tank (main tank) where the liquid originates. The chosen route must begin at this tank.

global_fields.name: target_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the destination tank (receiving tank). The chosen route must end at this tank.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_start_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Start (tail) tank ID for this directed pipeline segment. The segment allows flow from this tank to the segment_to_tank when its valve orientation is followed.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_end_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: End (head) tank ID for this directed pipeline segment. Flow through the segment arrives at this tank from segment_from_tank.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_id
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for this directed pipeline segment. This ID is used in the cost tables (base and interaction costs) to reference the segment but is not part of the route output (the route must list tanks only).

linear_item_fields.name: edge_id
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the pipeline segment to which the base (linear) transfer cost applies. Must match a segment_id defined in the pipeline segments list.

linear_item_fields.name: linear_cost
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Base transfer cost incurred if and only if the corresponding pipeline segment is used in the selected run. Sum these for every segment included in the route.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_i_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the first pipeline segment in a pairwise interaction term. Used together with segment_j_id to look up an additional fee incurred when both segments appear in the same run.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_j_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the second pipeline segment in a pairwise interaction term. Using both segment_i_id and segment_j_id in the chosen route triggers the listed interaction cost.

quadratic_item_fields.name: quadratic_cost
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Additional fee incurred if and only if both referenced pipeline segments are used in the route. Diagonal terms (segment_i_id == segment_j_id) represent a self-fee charged when that single segment is used.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct locations, junctions, or connection points in the garden map; used to gauge the size of the routing problem.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of directed hose/valve segments (one-way connections) available for routing water from supply to bed.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: List of all valid location identifiers (nodes) in the yard; the chosen route must be an ordered sequence of these location IDs.

global_fields.name: source_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the main water supply location where the hose route must start.

global_fields.name: target_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the flower bed location where the hose route must end.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_start_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Start (tail) location ID of a directed hose or valve segment — the location where that segment begins and water flows out of.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_end_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: End (head) location ID of a directed hose or valve segment — the location where that segment delivers water.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_id
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for this specific hose/valve segment. This ID is used only for referencing costs and must not appear in the final node-only route output.

linear_item_fields.name: edge_id
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the hose/valve segment whose base upkeep cost is being specified; must match a segment_id from the segments list.

linear_item_fields.name: linear_cost
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Base maintenance or upkeep cost incurred if and only if the corresponding hose/valve segment is used in the selected route.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_i_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the first hose/valve segment in a pairwise interaction cost term.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_j_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the second hose/valve segment in a pairwise interaction cost term.

quadratic_item_fields.name: quadratic_cost
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Additional cost incurred if both referenced segments are used in the route. Diagonal terms (same segment for i and j) represent a self-interaction cost; ordered pairs allow the extra charge to depend on which segment is considered first.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct junctions/locations in the water network map. These are the valid place identifiers the inspection team may list when giving their route.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of directed pipe segments (flow‑permitted connections) in the network. Each represents a one‑way physical segment the team can traverse.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Ordered list of all valid location (node) identifiers in the network. The chosen inspection path must be an ordered sequence of these location IDs starting at the entry valve and ending at the exit gate.

global_fields.name: source_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the entry valve location where the inspection team must start their single path.

global_fields.name: target_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the exit gate location where the inspection team must end their single path.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_start_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The tail node identifier: the junction/location where this directed pipe segment begins (where the team enters this segment).

edge_item_fields.name: edge_end_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The head node identifier: the junction/location where this directed pipe segment ends (where the team exits this segment).

edge_item_fields.name: edge_id
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for this pipe segment. This ID is used only to reference inspection times and pairwise penalties; it identifies a segment, not a node, and must not appear in the final node‑sequence output.

linear_item_fields.name: edge_id
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the pipe segment whose base inspection time is specified (must match an ID from the pipe segments list).

linear_item_fields.name: linear_cost
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Base inspection time (or cost) incurred if the team uses this pipe segment on their chosen route.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_i_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the first pipe segment in a pairwise penalty term. Used together with pipe_j_id to determine an extra penalty if both segments are inspected on the same route.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_j_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the second pipe segment in a pairwise penalty term. When both pipe_i_id and pipe_j_id are present on the chosen route their interaction penalty applies.

quadratic_item_fields.name: quadratic_cost
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Extra penalty (positive or negative) incurred when both referenced pipe segments are inspected on the same path. Diagonal entries (same pipe for i and j) represent an additional self‑penalty for using that single segment.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of distinct locations on the trail map (including the parking area and the lookout). This counts the places the photographer may visit along a route.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of directed trail segments (one-way paths) between locations. Each represents a permitted directed step the photographer can take.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: List of location identifiers (place names or IDs). The chosen route must be an ordered sequence of these location IDs starting at the parking area and ending at the lookout.

global_fields.name: source_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the starting location where the photographer begins (the parking area). The route must start at this node.

global_fields.name: target_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the destination location (the lookout). The route must end at this node.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_start_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The start location identifier (tail) of this directed trail segment — the place where the segment begins.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_end_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The end location identifier (head) of this directed trail segment — the place where the segment leads to.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_id
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for this directed trail segment. This ID links the segment to its linear effort cost and to quadratic interaction terms; it identifies an EDGE (a segment), not a location, and must not appear in the final route output.

linear_item_fields.name: edge_id
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Reference to the trail segment identifier (must match a segment_id from the edges list). Indicates which segment this linear effort applies to.

linear_item_fields.name: linear_cost
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Base tiredness/effort cost incurred if and only if the photographer takes this trail segment. This cost is added once per segment used on the chosen route.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_i_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the first trail segment in a pairwise interaction term. Used together with segment_j_id to specify an ordered interaction cost.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_j_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the second trail segment in a pairwise interaction term. The interaction is defined for ordered pairs (i,j).

quadratic_item_fields.name: quadratic_cost
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Additional tiredness penalty incurred if both referenced segments are taken on the route. For diagonal terms (i == j) this is the extra cost that applies when that single segment is included; for distinct segments the model uses ordered-pair terms, and the total interaction between two distinct segments is the sum of the (i,j) and (j,i) contributions when both are used.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct physical locations (rooms, intersections, or landmarks) in the building map. These are the nodes the student can be at while walking from the dorm to the lecture hall.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of directed corridor segments (one-way hallways) in the building. Each represents a usable corridor in a single allowed direction.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The list of valid location identifiers (names or IDs) for rooms, intersections, or other positions. A valid route is an ordered list chosen from these location IDs, starting at the dorm and ending at the lecture hall.

global_fields.name: source_node
global_fields.scenario_description: The location identifier where the student starts (the dorm). The chosen path must begin at this location.

global_fields.name: target_node
global_fields.scenario_description: The location identifier that is the student's destination (the lecture hall). The chosen path must end at this location.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_start_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The location identifier at the tail (start) of this directed corridor segment — where the student would be before taking this corridor.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_end_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The location identifier at the head (end) of this directed corridor segment — where the student arrives after traversing this corridor.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_id
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for this corridor segment (an ID that refers to the corridor itself, not a location). This ID is used by cost data to reference which corridor is used; corridor IDs must never appear in the final node-only path output.

linear_item_fields.name: edge_id
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: The corridor identifier that this base hassle entry refers to (must match a corridor_id listed in the corridors/edges section).

linear_item_fields.name: linear_cost
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: The basic hassle (base cost) incurred if and only if the student uses this corridor segment on the chosen route (e.g., distance, time, or inconvenience).

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_i_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: The corridor identifier for the first corridor in a pairwise interaction term. Interaction terms are ordered, so this is the first element in the ordered pair.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_j_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: The corridor identifier for the second corridor in a pairwise interaction term. If both corridor_i_id and corridor_j_id are used in the chosen route, the specified extra hassle is incurred; order matters, and diagonal entries model a corridor's extra self-contribution.

quadratic_item_fields.name: quadratic_cost
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: The additional hassle (interaction cost) incurred when both of the referenced corridors are used in the route. For an ordered pair (i,j) this is the extra cost contributed when corridor i and corridor j both appear; diagonal terms (i == j) represent an extra contribution from using that corridor on its own.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct scaffold locations or junctions on the map (includes pavement, intermediate platforms, and roof). Use this to know how many location IDs exist.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of directed scaffold segments (approved assembly pieces) that connect locations. Each segment is a one-way assembly step from one location to another.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: List of all valid location identifiers (node IDs) on the scaffold map. The chosen route must be an ordered sequence of these locations from ground to roof.

global_fields.name: source_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the starting location at ground level (the pavement). The selected path must begin at this location.

global_fields.name: target_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the final target location on the roof. The selected path must terminate at this location.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_start_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The tail location ID where this directed scaffold segment begins (the place where that segment is installed from). Consecutive locations in the output path must match segment_from_location -> segment_to_location pairs.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_end_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: The head location ID where this directed scaffold segment ends (the place where that segment arrives). This defines the allowed assembly direction for that segment.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_id
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for the directed scaffold segment. This ID is used only to reference costs (linear and quadratic); it must not appear in the final node-only route output.

linear_item_fields.name: edge_id
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the scaffold segment this linear cost applies to (must match a segment_id in the segments list).

linear_item_fields.name: linear_cost
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: The basic installation labor cost for this individual scaffold segment (this does not include the per-segment risk charge when that is represented as a quadratic diagonal). This cost is incurred if the segment is used in the chosen route.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_i_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the first scaffold segment in an ordered pair for which an interaction cost is specified. When both segments are used in the route (in any positions), this term may contribute; for ordered risks, both ordered entries are provided separately.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_j_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the second scaffold segment in an ordered pair for which an interaction cost is specified.

quadratic_item_fields.name: quadratic_cost
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Additional cost applied if both referenced segments are installed on the chosen route. Diagonal terms (first_segment_id == second_segment_id) represent the per-segment risk charge for installing that single segment; off-diagonal terms represent extra, order-sensitive combined risk when both segments appear (the pair's total contribution uses both ordered entries when segments are distinct).

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of physical locations (junctions, handholes, manholes, building or cabinet endpoints) in the conduit map. These are the node identifiers among which the route will be traced.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of directed conduit segments (allowed one-way conduit pieces) in the map. Each segment connects two locations and has its own fees and interaction costs.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: List of valid location identifiers (nodes). The chosen path must be an ordered sequence of these location IDs starting at the distribution cabinet and ending at the building.

global_fields.name: source_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Location ID of the distribution cabinet (the route origin). The solution path must start at this node.

global_fields.name: target_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Location ID of the destination building (the route endpoint). The solution path must end at this node.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_start_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Start (tail) location ID of a directed conduit segment. This is the location where that conduit segment departs.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_end_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: End (head) location ID of a directed conduit segment. This is the location where that conduit segment arrives.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_id
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier of this conduit segment. This ID is used to reference the segment's base fee and any pairwise interaction fees in the cost data (note: segment IDs are not to be output as part of the node path).

linear_item_fields.name: edge_id
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the conduit segment for which a base fee is specified. Must match a conduit_segment_id from the edges list.

linear_item_fields.name: linear_cost
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Base routing fee charged if and only if the corresponding conduit segment is included in the chosen route from the cabinet to the building.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_i_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the first conduit segment in an ordered interaction cost term. Used together with segment_j_id to indicate an extra charge if both segments are used.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_j_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the second conduit segment in an ordered interaction cost term. The interaction applies only when both this segment and segment_i_id are present on the chosen route.

quadratic_item_fields.name: quadratic_cost
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Additional fee applied when both specified conduit segments are used on the route. Diagonal terms (segment_i_id == segment_j_id) represent an extra surcharge applied when that single segment is used.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct physical locations on the production floor (nodes in the directed graph). These are places materials can be between processing stages.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of directed processing stages or transitions available (each directed edge represents a stage or processing step that moves the product from one location to another).

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Ordered list of valid location identifiers on the line (graph nodes). The chosen route must be a sequence of these locations starting at intake and ending at final assembly.

global_fields.name: source_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the raw-material intake location where the route must begin.

global_fields.name: target_node
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the finished-product or final assembly location where the route must end.

edge_item_fields.name: edge_start_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Location identifier where a specific processing stage begins (tail of the directed edge).

edge_item_fields.name: edge_end_node
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Location identifier where that processing stage ends (head of the directed edge).

edge_item_fields.name: edge_id
edge_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier of the directed processing stage (edge). This ID links the stage to its baseline cost and interaction costs; it is not a location and must not appear in the final location-only route output.

linear_item_fields.name: edge_id
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the processing stage (must match a stage_id from the edges list). Used to associate the baseline cost with that stage.

linear_item_fields.name: linear_cost
linear_item_fields.scenario_description: Baseline cost charged if and only if that processing stage is used in the chosen route (represents the stage's direct expense).

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_i_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the first processing stage in an interaction term. If this stage and the paired stage both appear on the route, the interaction cost applies.

quadratic_item_fields.name: edge_j_id
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the second processing stage in an interaction term. Together with stage_i_id it defines a pair whose joint use creates an additional charge.

quadratic_item_fields.name: quadratic_cost
quadratic_item_fields.scenario_description: Additional cost incurred when both referenced stages are included in the selected route. Diagonal terms (stage_i_id == stage_j_id) represent a stage's self-interaction (an extra single-stage charge). Off-diagonal terms are asymmetric and both directions are summed when both stages are used.
